sentences.zh: 志第三十刑法

translations.literal: Treatise 30: Penal Law
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 30: Penal Law

sentences.zh: 古之聖人，為人父母，莫不制禮以崇敬，立刑以明威，防閑于未然，懼爭心之將作也。

translations.literal: The ancient sages, as fathers and mothers of the people, all without exception established ritual to show reverence and set up punishments to display authority, guarding against misconduct before it arose, fearing that contentious hearts would soon stir.
translations.idiomatic: The sages of antiquity, in their role as fathers and mothers of the people, invariably instituted ritual to inspire reverence and established penal law to manifest authority, forestalling wrongdoing before it could take root, lest contentious hearts should soon arise.

sentences.zh: 故有輕重三典之異，宮墨五刑之差，度時而施宜，因事以議制。

translations.literal: Therefore there were the differences of the three codes in severity and lightness, and the distinctions of the five punishments of gong and mo, adapting measures to the times and deliberating institutions according to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the varying severity of the three canonical codes and the gradations of the five punishments, with measures adapted to the times and institutions shaped according to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 大則陳之原野，小則肆諸市朝，以禦奸宄，用懲禍亂。

translations.literal: For great offenses they were displayed in the open countryside; for lesser ones they were exposed in the marketplace and court, thereby to repel treachery and villainy and to punish calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Major offenses were punished in the open countryside; lesser ones in the marketplace and at court, all to repel treachery and villainy and to chastise calamity and disorder.

sentences.zh: 興邦致理，罔有弗由於此者也。

translations.literal: In raising a state and bringing about good order, there was nothing that did not proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: No state ever flourished in good order without relying upon this principle.

sentences.zh: 暨淳樸既消，澆偽斯起，刑增為九，章積三千，雖有凝脂次骨之峻，而錐刀之末，盡爭之矣。

translations.literal: When simplicity and honesty had vanished and decadence and falsity arose, punishments increased to nine and statutes accumulated to three thousand; though there were the severity of congealed fat and crushed bone, yet at the tip of an awl or knife-edge all strove over them.
translations.idiomatic: Once simplicity and honesty had faded and decadence and deceit had taken hold, punishments multiplied to nine categories and statutes piled up to three thousand articles. Even when penalties were as harsh as congealed fat and crushed bone, people still wrangled over every last awl-tip and knife-edge of the law.

sentences.zh: 自漢迄隋，世有增損，而罕能折衷。

translations.literal: From Han through Sui, each age had additions and reductions, yet few could strike a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han through the Sui, each dynasty added to or subtracted from the code, yet few ever achieved a balanced standard.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝參用周、齊舊政，以定律令，除苛慘之法，務在寬平。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui drew upon the old policies of Zhou and Qi to establish laws and ordinances, abolishing harsh and cruel methods and striving for leniency and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui drew on the old policies of the Northern Zhou and Northern Qi to codify laws and ordinances, abolishing harsh and cruel measures in favor of leniency and fairness.

sentences.zh: 比及晚年，漸亦滋虐。

translations.literal: By the time he reached his later years, he gradually became more oppressive as well.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, however, he gradually grew more oppressive.

sentences.zh: 煬帝忌刻，法令尤峻，人不堪命，遂至於亡。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was suspicious and harsh; laws and ordinances were especially severe; the people could not bear their lot, and thus the dynasty came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was suspicious and harsh; his laws and ordinances were especially severe. The people could not endure their lot, and the dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 高祖初起義師於太原，即布寬大之令。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor first raised his army of righteousness at Taiyuan, he immediately promulgated orders of leniency and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor first raised his army of righteousness at Taiyuan, he immediately issued orders of leniency and magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 百姓苦隋苛政，競來歸附。

translations.literal: The common people, suffering under the harsh government of Sui, vied with one another to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The common people, weary of the Sui's harsh rule, flocked to join him.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，遂成帝業。

translations.literal: Within a matter of months, he thus accomplished the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Within a matter of months he had accomplished the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 既平京城，約法為十二條。

translations.literal: After he had pacified the capital, he reduced the law to twelve articles.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the capital, he reduced the law to twelve articles.

sentences.zh: 惟制殺人、劫盜、背軍、叛逆者死，餘並蠲除之。

translations.literal: He ordained death only for murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion; all the rest he abolished entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He ordained death only for murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion; all other capital offenses were abolished.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，詔納言劉文靜與當朝通識之士，因開皇律令而損益之，盡削大業所用煩峻之法。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered the Counselor-in-Chief Liu Wenjing together with the learned men of the court to take the Kaihuang laws and ordinances as their basis and add or subtract from them, entirely cutting away the cumbersome and severe methods used in the Daye reign.
translations.idiomatic: Upon receiving the abdication, he ordered Counselor-in-Chief Liu Wenjing and the learned men of the court to revise the Kaihuang code, adding and subtracting as needed, and to abolish entirely the cumbersome and severe laws of the Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 又制五十三條格，務在寬簡，取便於時。

translations.literal: He also drew up fifty-three supplementary regulations, striving for leniency and simplicity and taking what was convenient for the times.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew up fifty-three supplementary regulations, aiming for leniency and simplicity and adapting to the needs of the moment.

sentences.zh: 尋又敕尚書左僕射裴寂、尚書右僕射蕭瑀及大理卿崔善為、給事中王敬業、中書舍人劉林甫顏師古王孝遠、涇州別駕靖延、太常丞丁孝烏、隋大理丞房軸、上將府參軍李桐客、太常博士徐上機等，撰定律令，大略以開皇為准。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he also commanded the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Ji, the Right Vice Director Xiao Yu, the Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Shannai, the Attendant within the Yellow Gate Wang Jingye, the Secretariat Drafters Liu Linpu, Yan Shigu, and Wang Xiaoyuan, the Vice Prefect of Jingzhou Jing Yan, the Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ding Xiaowu, the former Sui Director of Judicial Review Fang Zhou, the Staff Officer of the General-in-Chief's Office Li Tongke, the Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xu Shangji, and others to compile laws and ordinances, taking the Kaihuang code in general as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he also ordered Left Vice Director Pei Ji, Right Vice Director Xiao Yu, Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Shannai, Attendant Wang Jingye, Secretariat drafters Liu Linpu, Yan Shigu, and Wang Xiaoyuan, Jingzhou Vice Prefect Jing Yan, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Vice Director Ding Xiaowu, former Sui judicial review official Fang Zhou, General-in-Chief's staff officer Li Tongke, Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Xu Shangji, and others to compile laws and ordinances, taking the Kaihuang code as their general standard.

sentences.zh: 于時諸事始定，邊方尚梗，救時之弊，有所未暇，惟正五十三條格，入於新律，餘無所改。

translations.literal: At that time all affairs had only just been settled and the border regions were still obstructed; to remedy the ills of the age there were matters for which they had no leisure. They only corrected the fifty-three supplementary regulations and incorporated them into the new code; beyond this they made no changes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time affairs had only just been settled and the borderlands were still unsettled; pressing needs left no time for thorough revision. They corrected only the fifty-three supplementary regulations and incorporated them into the new code; nothing else was changed.

sentences.zh: 至武德七年五月奏上，乃下詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Wude it was submitted and approved, whereupon an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Wude it was submitted for approval, and an edict was issued, saying:

sentences.zh: 古不云乎，「萬邦之君，有典有則。

translations.literal: Did not the ancients say, "The lord of ten thousand states has canonical models and standards"?
translations.idiomatic: Did not the ancients say, "The lord of ten thousand states has canonical models and standards"?

sentences.zh: 」故九疇之敘，興于夏世，兩觀之法，大備隆周。

translations.literal: Therefore the ordering of the Nine Categories arose in the age of Xia, and the law of the Two Towers was fully perfected in the flourishing Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ordering of the Nine Categories arose in the Xia dynasty, and the law of the Two Towers was fully perfected in the flourishing Zhou.

sentences.zh: 所以禁暴懲奸，弘風闡化，安民立政，莫此為先。

translations.literal: Thus to restrain violence and punish villainy, to enlarge customs and unfold transformation, to settle the people and establish government—nothing takes precedence over this.
translations.idiomatic: To restrain violence and punish villainy, to enlarge customs and unfold civilization, to settle the people and establish government—nothing takes precedence over this.

sentences.zh: 自戰國紛擾，恃詐任力，苛制煩刑，於茲競起。

translations.literal: From the time when the Warring States were in turmoil, relying on deceit and trusting in force, harsh regulations and cumbersome punishments arose in competition with one another.
translations.idiomatic: From the turmoil of the Warring States onward, when men relied on deceit and trusted in brute force, harsh regulations and cumbersome punishments arose in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 秦並天下，隳滅禮教，恣行酷烈，害虐蒸民，宇內騷然，遂以顛覆。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm, destroyed ritual and teaching, and wantonly practiced cruelty and severity, harming and oppressing the common people until the realm was in turmoil and the dynasty was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Qin united the realm, destroyed ritual and teaching, and wantonly practiced cruelty and severity, harming and oppressing the common people until the realm was in turmoil and the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 漢氏撥亂，思易前軌，雖復務從約法，蠲削嚴刑，尚行菹醢之誅，猶設錙銖之禁。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty, in settling disorder, sought to change the former course; though they again strove to follow simplified law and abolished severe punishments, they still practiced the punishment of mincing and pickling, and still set up prohibitions as fine as a zhu or shu weight.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, in settling the chaos, sought to change the former course. Though they strove to simplify the law and abolish severe punishments, they still practiced the punishment of dismemberment and still set prohibitions as fine as a fraction of an ounce.

sentences.zh: 字民之道，實有未弘，刑措之風，以茲莫致。

translations.literal: The way of governing the people was in truth not yet broadly achieved, and the wind of setting punishments aside was thereby not attained.
translations.idiomatic: The way of governing the people was not yet fully realized, and the ideal of laying punishments aside was never achieved.

sentences.zh: 爰及魏、晉，流弊相沿，寬猛乖方，綱維失序。

translations.literal: Down to Wei and Jin, corrupt practices continued in succession; leniency and severity lost their proper alignment, and the guiding principles fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wei and Jin, corrupt practices continued in succession; leniency and severity lost their proper balance, and the guiding principles fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 下淩上替，政散民凋。

translations.literal: Inferiors overstepped superiors and the throne was usurped; government scattered and the people withered.
translations.idiomatic: Inferiors overstepped their superiors and the throne was usurped; government disintegrated and the people withered.

sentences.zh: 皆由法令湮訛，條章混謬。

translations.literal: All of this was because laws and ordinances had fallen into obscurity and error, and articles and regulations had become confused and mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: All of this stemmed from laws and ordinances that had fallen into obscurity and error, and from articles and regulations that had become confused and mistaken.

sentences.zh: 自斯以後，宇縣瓜分，戎馬交馳，未遑典制。

translations.literal: From this time onward the realm was carved up and war-horses galloped against one another; there was no leisure for canonical institutions.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward the realm was carved up and war-horses galloped against one another; there was no leisure to establish canonical institutions.

sentences.zh: 有隋之世，雖云厘革，然而損益不定，疏舛尚多，品式章程，罕能甄備。

translations.literal: In the age of Sui, though they were said to have reformed and changed, yet additions and subtractions were not settled, oversights and errors were still numerous, and categories, forms, and regulations could rarely be examined and made complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui dynasty, though reforms were undertaken, additions and subtractions were never settled, oversights and errors remained numerous, and categories, forms, and regulations could rarely be examined and made complete.

sentences.zh: 加以微文曲致，覽者惑其淺深，異例同科，用者殊其輕重，遂使奸吏巧詆，任情與奪，愚民妄觸，動陷羅網，屢聞厘革，卒以無成。

translations.literal: Moreover, with subtle wording and tortuous extensions, readers were confused as to their depth or shallowness; different precedents were placed in the same category, and those who applied them made the severity and leniency different. Thus crafty clerks ingeniously twisted the law and arbitrarily granted or withheld punishment; foolish commoners rashly transgressed and constantly fell into the net. Repeatedly they heard of reforms and changes, yet in the end nothing was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, subtle wording and tortuous extensions confused readers as to their meaning; different precedents were lumped into the same category, and those who applied the law made severity and leniency vary at will. Crafty clerks twisted the law and arbitrarily granted or withheld punishment; foolish commoners rashly transgressed and constantly fell into the net. Reforms were repeatedly announced, yet in the end nothing was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 朕膺期受籙，甯濟區宇，永言至治，興寐為勞。

translations.literal: We have received the mandate at the appointed season and bring peace to the realm; ever speaking of supreme governance, We rise from sleep and lie down in toil.
translations.idiomatic: We have received the mandate at the appointed season and bring peace to the realm; ever mindful of supreme governance, We rise from sleep and lie down in toil.

sentences.zh: 補千年之墜典，拯百王之餘弊，思所以正本澄源，式清流末，永垂憲則，貽範後昆。

translations.literal: We repair the fallen canons of a thousand years and rescue the remaining defects of a hundred kings, thinking how to rectify the root and clarify the source, to set the pattern for purifying the downstream current, to hand down constitutional norms forever, and to bequeath a model to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: We repair the fallen canons of a thousand years and rescue the remaining defects of a hundred kings, seeking to rectify the root and clarify the source, to set a pattern for purifying what flows downstream, to hand down constitutional norms forever, and to bequeath a model to posterity.

sentences.zh: 爰命群才，修定科律。

translations.literal: We therefore command the assembled talents to revise and fix the statutes and laws.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore command the assembled talents to revise and fix the statutes and laws.

sentences.zh: 但今古異務，文質不同，喪亂之後，事殊曩代，應機適變，救弊斯在。

translations.literal: Yet ancient and modern affairs differ, and ornament and substance are not the same; after the age of ruin and disorder, matters are unlike former generations. To respond to the moment and adapt to change, to remedy defects—herein lies the need.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ancient and modern affairs differ, and ornament and substance are not the same; after the age of ruin and disorder, matters are unlike former generations. To respond to the moment and adapt to change, to remedy defects—herein lies the need.

sentences.zh: 是以斟酌繁省，取合時宜，矯正差遺，務從體要。

translations.literal: Therefore We weigh what is cumbersome and what is simplified, taking what accords with the timely fit, correcting discrepancies and oversights, and striving to follow the essential substance.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We weigh what is cumbersome and what is simplified, taking what accords with the needs of the time, correcting discrepancies and oversights, and striving to follow the essential substance.

sentences.zh: 迄茲曆稔，撰次始畢，宜下四方，即令頒用。

translations.literal: Until now several years have passed and the compilation is at last complete; it should be sent down to the four quarters and immediately ordered into use.
translations.idiomatic: Several years have now passed and the compilation is at last complete; it should be sent down to the four quarters and immediately put into use.

sentences.zh: 庶使吏曹簡肅，無取懸石之多；

translations.literal: We hope thereby to make the offices of clerks simple and orderly, not taking on the multitude of a hanging stone's weight;
translations.idiomatic: We hope thereby to make the offices of clerks simple and orderly, not burdened with the weight of a hanging stone;

sentences.zh: 奏讞平允，靡競錐刀之末。

translations.literal: and to make presented judgments fair and even, with no competing over the tip of an awl or knife-edge.
translations.idiomatic: and to make presented judgments fair and even, with no wrangling over the tip of an awl or knife-edge of the law.

sentences.zh: 勝殘去殺，此焉非遠。

translations.literal: To overcome the cruel and remove killing—this is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: To overcome cruelty and abolish killing—this is not far off.

sentences.zh: 於是頒行天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，又命長孫無忌、房玄齡與學士法官，更加厘改。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he again ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and the academicians and judicial officials to revise it further.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he again ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and the academicians and judicial officials to revise the code further.

sentences.zh: 戴胄、魏徵又言舊律令重，于時議絞刑之屬五十條。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou and Wei Zheng also said that the old laws and ordinances were heavy; at that time they deliberated on fifty articles belonging to the category of strangulation and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou and Wei Zheng also argued that the old laws and ordinances were too severe; at that time they deliberated on fifty articles involving strangulation and similar capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 免死罪，斷其右趾，應死者多蒙全活。

translations.literal: Exempting them from the death penalty, they cut off the right foot; of those who should have died, many received full preservation of life.
translations.idiomatic: They exempted these offenders from the death penalty and instead cut off the right foot; of those who should have died, many were spared.

sentences.zh: 太宗尋又湣其受刑之苦，謂侍臣曰：「前代不行肉刑久矣，今忽斷人右趾，意甚不忍。

translations.literal: Before long Taizong again pitied their suffering under punishment and said to his attendant ministers: "Former ages have not practiced corporal punishment for a long time; now suddenly to cut off a person's right foot—Our mind is deeply unwilling."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Taizong again pitied their suffering under punishment and said to his attendant ministers: "Former ages have not practiced corporal punishment for a long time; now suddenly to cut off a person's right foot—Our mind is deeply unwilling."

sentences.zh: 」諫議大夫王珪對曰：「古行肉刑，以為輕罪。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Counselor Wang Gui replied: "In antiquity corporal punishment was practiced for what were considered light offenses."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Wang Gui replied: "In antiquity corporal punishment was practiced for what were considered light offenses."

sentences.zh: 今陛下矜死刑之多，設斷趾之法，格本合死，今而獲生。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, taking pity on the multitude of death sentences, established the law of cutting off the foot; those who by the standard should die now obtain life.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty, taking pity on the multitude of death sentences, established the law of cutting off the foot; those who by the standard should die now obtain life.

sentences.zh: 刑者幸得全命，豈憚去其一足？

translations.literal: Those punished are fortunate to preserve their lives entirely—how would they fear losing one foot?
translations.idiomatic: Those punished are fortunate to preserve their lives—how would they fear losing one foot?

sentences.zh: 且人之見者，甚足懲誡。

translations.literal: Moreover, for those who see it, it is quite sufficient as warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for those who witness it, the punishment is quite sufficient as a warning.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「本以為寬，故行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "We originally thought it lenient, and therefore put it into practice."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "We originally thought it lenient, and therefore put it into practice."

sentences.zh: 然每聞惻愴，不能忘懷。

translations.literal: Yet whenever We hear of it We are filled with compassion and cannot put it from Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever We hear of it We are filled with compassion and cannot put it from Our mind.

sentences.zh: 」又謂蕭瑀、陳叔達等曰：「朕以死者不可再生，思有矜湣，故簡死罪五十條，從斷右趾。

translations.literal: He also said to Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, and others: "We, thinking that the dead cannot be brought back to life and wishing to show compassion, therefore selected fifty death-penalty articles and substituted cutting off the right foot."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, and others: "We, thinking that the dead cannot be brought back to life and wishing to show compassion, therefore selected fifty death-penalty articles and substituted cutting off the right foot."

sentences.zh: 朕復念其受痛，極所不忍。

translations.literal: We again reflect on their suffering pain and are utterly unwilling.
translations.idiomatic: We again reflect on their suffering and are utterly unwilling to inflict such pain.

sentences.zh: 」叔達等咸曰：「古之肉刑，乃在死刑之外。

translations.literal: Shuda and the others all said: "The corporal punishments of antiquity were applied beyond the death penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Shuda and the others all said: "The corporal punishments of antiquity were applied in addition to the death penalty."

sentences.zh: 陛下于死刑之內，改從斷趾，便是以生易死，足為寬法。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, within the death penalty, changed it to cutting off the foot instead—this is to exchange life for death and is fully sufficient as a lenient law.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, within the death penalty, substituted cutting off the foot—this is to exchange life for death and is fully sufficient as a lenient law.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕意以為如此，故欲行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Our mind thought it thus, and therefore We wished to put it into practice."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Our mind thought it thus, and therefore We wished to put it into practice."

sentences.zh: 又有上書言此非便，公可更思之。

translations.literal: There was also a memorial saying this was not convenient; you may reconsider it."
translations.idiomatic: There was also a memorial saying this was not convenient; you may reconsider it."

sentences.zh: 」其後蜀王法曹參軍裴弘獻又駁律令不便於時者四十餘事，太宗令參掌刪改之。

translations.literal: Thereafter Pei Hongxian, Legal Bureau Staff Officer under the Prince of Shu, again refuted more than forty matters in the laws and ordinances that were inconvenient for the times, and Taizong ordered him to participate in supervising their deletion and revision.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Pei Hongxian, Legal Bureau staff officer under the Prince of Shu, again refuted more than forty matters in the laws and ordinances that were inconvenient for the times, and Taizong ordered him to participate in revising them.

sentences.zh: 弘獻於是與玄齡等建議，以為古者五刑，刖居其一。

translations.literal: Hongxian thereupon joined Xuanling and the others in proposing that in antiquity there were five punishments, of which amputation of the foot was one.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxian thereupon joined Xuanling and the others in proposing that in antiquity there were five punishments, of which amputation of the foot was one.

sentences.zh: 及肉刑廢，制為死、流、杖、笞凡五等，以備五刑。

translations.literal: When corporal punishment was abolished, they established death, exile, beating with the staff, and beating with the rod—altogether five grades—to replace the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When corporal punishment was abolished, they established death, exile, beating with the staff, and beating with the rod—altogether five grades—to replace the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 今復設刖足，昌為六刑。

translations.literal: Now to establish again the cutting off of the foot is to make six punishments in error.
translations.idiomatic: Now to establish again the cutting off of the foot is to make six punishments in error.

sentences.zh: 減死在於寬弘，加刑又加煩峻。

translations.literal: Reducing death lies in leniency and magnanimity; adding a punishment again adds to severity and cumbersomeness.
translations.idiomatic: Reducing death lies in leniency and magnanimity; adding a punishment again adds severity and cumbersomeness.

sentences.zh: 乃與八座定議奏聞，於是又除斷趾法，改為加役流三千里，居作二年。

translations.literal: They then joined the Eight Seats in fixing the deliberation and submitting it for report; thereupon the law of cutting off the foot was again abolished and changed to penal servitude exile for three thousand li with two years of labor.
translations.idiomatic: They then joined the Eight Seats in fixing the deliberation and submitting it for report; thereupon the law of cutting off the foot was abolished and changed to penal servitude exile for three thousand li with two years of labor.

sentences.zh: 又舊條疏，兄弟分後，廕不相及，連坐俱死，祖孫配沒。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the old commentaries on the articles, when brothers had divided their household, hereditary privilege did not extend to one another; collective punishment meant all were put to death, while grandparents and grandchildren were sentenced to confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the old commentaries on the articles, when brothers had divided their household, hereditary privilege did not extend to one another; collective punishment meant all were put to death, while grandparents and grandchildren were sentenced to confiscation.

sentences.zh: 會有同州人房強，弟任統軍於岷州，以謀反伏誅，強當從坐。

translations.literal: It happened that Fang Qiang of Tongzhou had a younger brother serving as army commander at Minzhou who was executed for plotting rebellion; Qiang was subject to collective punishment.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Fang Qiang of Tongzhou had a younger brother serving as army commander at Minzhou who was executed for plotting rebellion; Qiang was subject to collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗錄囚徒，憫其將死，為之動容。

translations.literal: Taizong once reviewed prisoners and pitied those about to die, his countenance moved for them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once reviewed prisoners and pitied those about to die; his countenance was moved for them.

sentences.zh: 顧謂侍臣曰：「刑典仍用，蓋風化未洽之咎。

translations.literal: Turning to his attendant ministers he said: "That the penal code is still in use is surely the fault of customs and transformation not yet being harmonized."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendant ministers he said: "That the penal code is still in use is surely the fault of customs and transformation not yet being harmonized."

sentences.zh: 愚人何罪，而肆重刑乎？

translations.literal: What crime have foolish men committed, that heavy punishments are applied so freely?
translations.idiomatic: What crime have foolish men committed, that heavy punishments are applied so freely?

sentences.zh: 更彰朕之不德也。

translations.literal: This further displays Our lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This further displays Our lack of virtue.

sentences.zh: 用刑之道，當審事理之輕重，然後加之以刑罰。

translations.literal: The way of applying punishments should examine the lightness or heaviness of the matter and principle, and only then add punishments upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The way of applying punishments should examine the lightness or heaviness of the offense, and only then impose penalties.

sentences.zh: 何有不察其本而一概加誅，非所以恤刑重人命也。

translations.literal: How can one fail to examine the root and apply execution indiscriminately? This is not the way to show compassion in punishment and value human life.
translations.idiomatic: How can one fail to examine the root of the matter and apply execution indiscriminately? This is not the way to show compassion in punishment and value human life.

sentences.zh: 然則反逆有二：一為興師動眾，一為惡言犯法。

translations.literal: Thus rebellion has two kinds: one is raising troops and moving the masses; one is evil words violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion has two kinds: one is raising troops and moving the masses; the other is evil words violating the law.

sentences.zh: 輕重有差，而連坐皆死，豈朕情之所安哉？

translations.literal: In severity and leniency there is a difference, yet collective punishment puts all to death—how can this be what Our mind finds acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: In severity and leniency there is a difference, yet collective punishment puts all to death—how can this be what Our mind finds acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」更令百僚詳議。

translations.literal: He again ordered the hundred officials to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He again ordered the hundred officials to deliberate in detail.

sentences.zh: 於是玄齡等復定議曰：「案禮，孫為王父屍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuanling and the others again fixed the deliberation, saying: "According to the Rites, the grandson serves as the corpse for the grandfather."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xuanling and the others again fixed the deliberation, saying: "According to the Rites, the grandson serves as the corpse for the grandfather."

sentences.zh: 案令，祖有廕孫之義。

translations.literal: According to the Ordinances, the grandfather has the meaning of hereditary privilege for the grandson.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Ordinances, the grandfather has the meaning of hereditary privilege for the grandson.

sentences.zh: 然則祖孫親重而兄弟屬輕，應重反流，合輕翻死，據禮論情，深為未愜。

translations.literal: Thus the bond between grandfather and grandson is heavy in closeness while the tie between brothers is light in category; what should be heavy is reversed to exile, while what should be light is reversed to death. Judging by ritual and weighing by feeling, this is deeply unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the bond between grandfather and grandson is closer in kinship while the tie between brothers is lighter; what should be heavy is reversed to exile, while what should be light is reversed to death. Judging by ritual and weighing by feeling, this is deeply unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 今定律，祖孫與兄弟緣坐，俱配沒。

translations.literal: Now in fixing the law, grandparents and grandchildren together with brothers, through collective punishment, are all sentenced to confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Now in fixing the law, grandparents and grandchildren together with brothers, through collective punishment, are all sentenced to confiscation.

sentences.zh: 其以惡言犯法不能為害者，情狀稍輕，兄弟免死，配流為允。

translations.literal: For those who through evil words violate the law but cannot cause harm, the circumstances are somewhat lighter; exempting brothers from death and sentencing them to exile and confiscation is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: For those who through evil words violate the law but cannot cause harm, the circumstances are somewhat lighter; exempting brothers from death and sentencing them to exile and confiscation is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 自是比古死刑，殆除其半。

translations.literal: From this time, compared with the death penalties of antiquity, nearly half were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, compared with the death penalties of antiquity, nearly half were abolished.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等遂與法司定律五百條，分為十二卷：一曰名例，二曰衛禁，三曰職制，四曰戶婚，五曰廄庫，六曰擅興，七曰賊盜，八曰鬥訟，九曰詐偽，十曰雜律，十一曰捕亡，十二曰斷獄。

translations.literal: Xuanling and the others thereupon joined the judicial offices in fixing five hundred articles of law, divided into twelve scrolls: first, General Principles; second, Imperial Guard and Prohibitions; third, Official Regulations; fourth, Households and Marriage; fifth, Stables and Storehouses; sixth, Unauthorized Mobilization; seventh, Banditry and Theft; eighth, Assault and Litigation; ninth, Fraud and Forgery; tenth, Miscellaneous Statutes; eleventh, Apprehension of Fugitives; twelfth, Trial and Judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and the others thereupon joined the judicial offices in fixing five hundred articles of law, divided into twelve scrolls: General Principles; Imperial Guard and Prohibitions; Official Regulations; Households and Marriage; Stables and Storehouses; Unauthorized Mobilization; Banditry and Theft; Assault and Litigation; Fraud and Forgery; Miscellaneous Statutes; Apprehension of Fugitives; and Trial and Judgment.

sentences.zh: 有笞、杖、徒、流、死，為五刑。

translations.literal: There were beating with the rod, beating with the staff, penal servitude, exile, and death—the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: There were beating with the rod, beating with the staff, penal servitude, exile, and death—the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 笞刑五條，自笞十至五十；

translations.literal: Rod punishment had five articles, from ten strokes to fifty;
translations.idiomatic: Rod punishment had five grades, from ten strokes to fifty;

sentences.zh: 杖刑五條，自杖六十至杖一百；

translations.literal: staff punishment had five articles, from sixty strokes to one hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Staff punishment had five grades, from sixty strokes to one hundred;

sentences.zh: 徒刑五條，自徒一年，遞加半年，至三年；

translations.literal: servitude punishment had five articles, from one year of servitude, increasing by half a year each step, up to three years;
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude had five grades, from one year, increasing by half a year each step, up to three years;

sentences.zh: 流刑三條，自流二千里，遞加五百里，至三千里；

translations.literal: exile punishment had three articles, from exile for two thousand li, increasing by five hundred li each step, up to three thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Exile had three grades, from two thousand li, increasing by five hundred li each step, up to three thousand li;

sentences.zh: 死刑二條：絞、斬。

translations.literal: death penalty had two articles: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The death penalty had two forms: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 大凡二十等。

translations.literal: In all there were twenty grades.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were twenty grades.

sentences.zh: 又有議請減贖當免之法八：一曰議親，二曰議故，三曰議賢，四曰議能，五曰議功，六曰議貴，七曰議賓，八曰議勤。

translations.literal: There were also eight methods of deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation, and exemption: first, deliberation for kin; second, deliberation for old associates; third, deliberation for worthies; fourth, deliberation for ability; fifth, deliberation for merit; sixth, deliberation for nobility; seventh, deliberation for guests; eighth, deliberation for diligence.
translations.idiomatic: There were also eight methods of deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation, and exemption: deliberation for kin; for old associates; for worthies; for ability; for merit; for nobility; for guests; and for diligence.

sentences.zh: 八議者，犯死罪者皆條所坐及應議之狀奏請，議定奏裁。

translations.literal: For the Eight Deliberations, all who committed death-penalty crimes were to set forth the offense charged and the circumstances warranting deliberation in a memorial petition; after deliberation was fixed, it was submitted for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eight Deliberations, all who committed capital offenses were to set forth the offense charged and the circumstances warranting deliberation in a memorial petition; after deliberation was concluded, the case was submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 流罪已下，減一等。

translations.literal: For offenses of exile and below, one grade was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For offenses of exile and below, one grade was reduced.

sentences.zh: 若官爵五品已上，及皇太子妃大功已上親，應議者周以上親，犯死罪者上請。

translations.literal: If one held official rank of the fifth grade or above, or was a relative within great-achievement mourning of the crown prince's consort, or was a relative within the Zhou mourning circle who qualified for deliberation, and committed a death-penalty offense, a petition was submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: If one held official rank of the fifth grade or above, or was a relative within great-achievement mourning of the crown prince's consort, or was a relative within the Zhou mourning circle who qualified for deliberation, and committed a capital offense, a petition was submitted upward.

sentences.zh: 流罪已下，亦減一等。

translations.literal: For offenses of exile and below, one grade was also reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For offenses of exile and below, one grade was also reduced.

sentences.zh: 若七品已上官，及官爵得請者之祖父母、父母、兄弟、姊妹、妻、子孫，犯流罪已下，各減一等。

translations.literal: If one was an official of the seventh grade or above, or the grandparents, parents, brothers, sisters, wife, and descendants of one whose official rank qualified for petition, and they committed offenses of exile and below, each had one grade reduced.
translations.idiomatic: If one was an official of the seventh grade or above, or the grandparents, parents, brothers, sisters, wife, and descendants of one whose official rank qualified for petition, and they committed offenses of exile and below, each had one grade reduced.

sentences.zh: 若應議請減及九品已上官，若官品得減者之祖父母、父母、妻、子孫，犯流罪已下，聽贖。

translations.literal: If one qualified for deliberation, petition, or reduction, or was an official of the ninth grade or above, or the grandparents, parents, wife, and descendants of one whose official rank qualified for reduction, and they committed offenses of exile and below, commutation was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If one qualified for deliberation, petition, or reduction, or was an official of the ninth grade or above, or the grandparents, parents, wife, and descendants of one whose official rank qualified for reduction, and they committed offenses of exile and below, commutation was permitted.

sentences.zh: 其贖法：笞十，贖銅一斤，遞加一斤，至杖一百，則贖銅十斤。

translations.literal: The commutation method: for ten strokes of the rod, one jin of copper was commuted; increasing by one jin each step, up to one hundred strokes of the staff, which commuted ten jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: The commutation method: for ten strokes of the rod, one jin of copper; increasing by one jin each step, up to one hundred strokes of the staff, which commuted to ten jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 自此已上，遞加十斤，至徒三年，則贖銅六十斤。

translations.literal: From this upward, increasing by ten jin each step, up to three years of servitude, which commuted sixty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: From this upward, increasing by ten jin each step, up to three years of penal servitude, which commuted to sixty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 流二千里者，贖銅八十斤；

translations.literal: For exile of two thousand li, eighty jin of copper was commuted;
translations.idiomatic: For exile of two thousand li, eighty jin of copper;

sentences.zh: 流二千五百里者，贖銅九十斤；

translations.literal: for exile of two thousand five hundred li, ninety jin of copper;
translations.idiomatic: for exile of two thousand five hundred li, ninety jin of copper;

sentences.zh: 流三千里者，贖銅一百斤。

translations.literal: for exile of three thousand li, one hundred jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: for exile of three thousand li, one hundred jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 絞斬者，贖銅一百二十斤。

translations.literal: For strangulation and decapitation, one hundred twenty jin of copper was commuted.
translations.idiomatic: For strangulation and decapitation, one hundred twenty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 又許以官當罪。

translations.literal: They also permitted using office to offset punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They also permitted using official rank to offset punishment.

sentences.zh: 以官當徒者，五品已上犯私罪者，一官當徒二年；

translations.literal: For using office to offset penal servitude, those of the fifth grade and above who committed private offenses had one office offset two years of servitude;
translations.idiomatic: For using office to offset penal servitude, those of the fifth grade and above who committed private offenses had one office offset two years of servitude;

sentences.zh: 九品已上，一官當徒一年。

translations.literal: those of the ninth grade and above had one office offset one year of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: those of the ninth grade and above had one office offset one year of servitude.

sentences.zh: 若犯公罪者，各加一年。

translations.literal: If they committed public offenses, each added one year.
translations.idiomatic: If they committed public offenses, each added one year.

sentences.zh: 以官當流者，三流同比徒四年，仍各解見任。

translations.literal: For using office to offset exile, the three grades of exile together equaled four years of servitude, and each still had their current appointment removed.
translations.idiomatic: For using office to offset exile, the three grades of exile together equaled four years of servitude, and each still had their current appointment removed.

sentences.zh: 除名者，比徒三年。

translations.literal: Removal from the register was equivalent to three years of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Removal from the register was equivalent to three years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 免官者，比徒二年。

translations.literal: Dismissal from office was equivalent to two years of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissal from office was equivalent to two years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 免所居官者，比徒一年。

translations.literal: Removal from the office held was equivalent to one year of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Removal from the office held was equivalent to one year of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 又有十惡之條：一曰謀反，二曰謀大逆，三曰謀叛，四曰謀惡逆，五曰不道，六曰大不敬，七曰不孝，八曰不睦，九曰不義，十曰內亂。

translations.literal: There were also the Ten Abominations: first, plotting rebellion; second, plotting great treason; third, plotting defection; fourth, plotting wicked rebellion; fifth, unnatural conduct; sixth, great irreverence; seventh, unfilial conduct; eighth, discord within the clan; ninth, unrighteous conduct; tenth, internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Ten Abominations: plotting rebellion; plotting great treason; plotting defection; plotting wicked rebellion; unnatural conduct; great irreverence; unfilial conduct; discord within the clan; unrighteous conduct; and internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 其犯十惡者，不得依議請之例。

translations.literal: Those who committed the Ten Abominations could not rely on the precedents of deliberation and petition.
translations.idiomatic: Those who committed the Ten Abominations could not rely on the precedents of deliberation and petition.

sentences.zh: 年七十以上、十五以下及廢疾，犯流罪以下，亦聽贖。

translations.literal: Those seventy years and above, fifteen and below, and the disabled, who committed offenses of exile and below, were also permitted commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Those seventy years and above, fifteen and below, and the disabled, who committed offenses of exile and below, were also permitted commutation.

sentences.zh: 八十已上、十歲以下及篤疾，犯反逆殺人應死者，上請，盜及傷人，亦收贖，餘皆勿論。

translations.literal: Those eighty and above, ten years and below, and the gravely disabled, who committed rebellion, treason, or murder warranting death, submitted petitions upward; for theft and wounding others, commutation was also accepted; all else was not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Those eighty and above, ten years and below, and the gravely disabled, who committed rebellion, treason, or murder warranting death, submitted petitions upward; for theft and wounding others, commutation was also accepted; all else was not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 九十以上、七歲以下，雖有死罪，不加刑。

translations.literal: Those ninety and above and seven and below, though they had death-penalty crimes, were not subjected to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those ninety and above and seven and below, though they had capital offenses, were not subjected to punishment.

sentences.zh: 比隋代舊律，減大辟者九十二條，減流入徒者七十一條。

translations.literal: Compared with the old code of the Sui dynasty, ninety-two articles reducing the great execution were cut, and seventy-one articles reducing exile to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the old Sui code, ninety-two articles reducing capital punishment were cut, and seventy-one articles reducing exile to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 其當徒之法，唯奪一官，除名之人，仍同士伍。

translations.literal: The method of offsetting servitude stripped only one office; those removed from the register were still treated the same as common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The method of offsetting servitude stripped only one office; those removed from the register were still treated the same as common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 凡削煩去蠹，變重為輕者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In all, the cutting of cumbersomeness and removal of harm, changing the heavy to the light, could not be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the cutting of cumbersomeness and removal of harm, changing the heavy to the light, could not be fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 又定令一千五百九十條，為三十卷。

translations.literal: They also fixed one thousand five hundred ninety articles of ordinances in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: They also fixed one thousand five hundred ninety articles of ordinances in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年正月，頒下之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year of Zhenguan it was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year of Zhenguan it was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 又刪武德、貞觀已來敕格三千餘件，定留七百條，以為格十八卷，留本司施行。

translations.literal: They also deleted more than three thousand imperial edicts and regulations since Wude and Zhenguan, fixing seven hundred articles to remain, making them into eighteen scrolls of regulations to be kept and implemented by the original bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: They also deleted more than three thousand imperial edicts and regulations since Wude and Zhenguan, retaining seven hundred articles in eighteen scrolls of regulations to be kept and implemented by the original bureaus.

sentences.zh: 斟酌今古，除煩去弊，甚為寬簡，便於人者。

translations.literal: Weighing ancient and modern, removing cumbersomeness and eliminating defects, it was very lenient and simple and convenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing ancient and modern, removing cumbersomeness and eliminating defects, it was very lenient and simple and convenient for the people.

sentences.zh: 以尚書省諸曹為之目，初為七卷。

translations.literal: Taking the various bureaus of the Department of State Affairs as its categories, it was at first seven scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the various bureaus of the Department of State Affairs as its categories, it was at first seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其曹之常條，但留本司者，別為《留司格》一卷。

translations.literal: The standing articles of each bureau that were kept only by the original bureau were separately made into one scroll of Retained Bureau Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The standing articles of each bureau that were kept only by the original bureau were separately compiled as one scroll of Retained Bureau Regulations.

sentences.zh: 蓋編錄當時制敕，永為法則，以為故事。

translations.literal: This was compiling the regulations and edicts of the time, making them forever constitutional norms and taking them as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This compiled the regulations and edicts of the time, making them forever constitutional norms and taking them as precedent.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀格》十八卷，房玄齡等刪定。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Regulations in eighteen scrolls were revised and fixed by Fang Xuanling and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Regulations in eighteen scrolls were revised and fixed by Fang Xuanling and others.

sentences.zh: 《永徽留司格》十八卷，《散頒格》七卷，長孫無忌等刪定，永徽中，又令源直心等刪定，惟改易官號曹局之名，不易篇目。

translations.literal: The Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations in eighteen scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in seven scrolls were revised and fixed by Zhangsun Wuji and others; in the Yonghui reign, Yuan Zhixin and others were again ordered to revise and fix them, only changing the names of official titles and bureau offices, not altering the section titles.
translations.idiomatic: The Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations in eighteen scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in seven scrolls were revised by Zhangsun Wuji and others; in the Yonghui reign, Yuan Zhixin and others were again ordered to revise them, only changing the names of official titles and bureau offices, not altering the section titles.

sentences.zh: 《永徽留司格後本》，劉仁軌等刪定。

translations.literal: The Later Edition of the Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations was revised and fixed by Liu Rengui and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Edition of the Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations was revised by Liu Rengui and others.

sentences.zh: 《垂拱留司格》六卷，《散頒格》三卷，裴居道刪定。

translations.literal: The Chuigong Retained Bureau Regulations in six scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in three scrolls were revised and fixed by Pei Judao.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuigong Retained Bureau Regulations in six scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in three scrolls were revised by Pei Judao.

sentences.zh: 《太極格》十卷，岑羲等刪定。

translations.literal: The Taiji Regulations in ten scrolls were revised and fixed by Cen Xi and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiji Regulations in ten scrolls were revised by Cen Xi and others.

sentences.zh: 《開元前格》十卷，姚崇等刪定。

translations.literal: The Pre-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were revised and fixed by Yao Chong and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Pre-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were revised by Yao Chong and others.

sentences.zh: 《開元後格》十卷，宋璟等刪定。

translations.literal: The Post-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were revised and fixed by Song Jing and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Post-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were revised by Song Jing and others.

sentences.zh: 皆以尚書省二十四司為篇目。

translations.literal: All took the twenty-four bureaus of the Department of State Affairs as section titles.
translations.idiomatic: All took the twenty-four bureaus of the Department of State Affairs as section titles.

sentences.zh: 凡式三十有三篇，亦以尚書省列曹及秘書、太常、司農、光祿、太僕、太府、少府及監門、宿衛、計帳名其篇目，為二十卷。

translations.literal: In all there were thirty-three sections of forms, also naming their section titles from the listed bureaus of the Department of State Affairs and the Secretariat, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of the National Granaries, Court of the Imperial Stud, Court of the Imperial Carriages, Court of the Imperial Treasury, Court of the Imperial Manufactories, and the Directorate of Gatekeepers, Palace Guards, and Accounting, making twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were thirty-three sections of forms, also naming their section titles from the listed bureaus of the Department of State Affairs and the Secretariat, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of the National Granaries, Court of the Imperial Stud, Court of the Imperial Carriages, Court of the Imperial Treasury, Court of the Imperial Manufactories, and the Directorates of Gatekeepers, Palace Guards, and Accounting, making twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《永徽式》十四卷，《垂拱》、《神龍》、《開元式》並二十卷，其刪定格令同。

translations.literal: The Yonghui Forms in fourteen scrolls, and the Chuigong, Shenlong, and Kaiyuan Forms each in twenty scrolls—their revision and fixing of regulations and ordinances was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Yonghui Forms in fourteen scrolls, and the Chuigong, Shenlong, and Kaiyuan Forms each in twenty scrolls—their revision of regulations and ordinances followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 太宗又制在京見禁囚，刑部每月一奏，從立春至秋分，不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: Taizong also ordained that for prisoners detained in the capital, the Ministry of Justice should report once a month; from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox, death sentences could not be reported and decided.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also ordained that for prisoners detained in the capital, the Ministry of Justice should report once a month; from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox, death sentences could not be reported and decided.

sentences.zh: 其大祭祀及致齋、朔望、上下弦、二十四氣、雨未晴、夜未明、斷屠日月及假日，並不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: On great sacrifices and days of ritual abstinence, new and full moons, first and third quarter moons, the twenty-four seasonal nodes, days when rain had not cleared, nights when dawn had not come, days of prohibition on slaughter, and holidays, death sentences likewise could not be reported and decided.
translations.idiomatic: On great sacrifices and days of ritual abstinence, new and full moons, first and third quarter moons, the twenty-four seasonal nodes, days when rain had not cleared, nights when dawn had not come, days of prohibition on slaughter, and holidays, death sentences likewise could not be reported and decided.

sentences.zh: 其有赦之日，武庫令設金雞及鼓于宮城門外之右，勒集囚徒于闕前，撾鼓千聲訖，宣詔而釋之。

translations.literal: On days when there was an amnesty, the Director of the Armory set up a golden rooster and drum to the right outside the palace-city gate, assembled the prisoners before the gate-tower, and when a thousand drumbeats had finished, proclaimed the edict and released them.
translations.idiomatic: On days when there was an amnesty, the Director of the Armory set up a golden rooster and drum to the right outside the palace-city gate, assembled the prisoners before the gate-tower, and when a thousand drumbeats had finished, proclaimed the edict and released them.

sentences.zh: 其赦書頒諸州，用絹寫行下。

translations.literal: The amnesty document was promulgated to the prefectures, written on silk and sent down.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty document was promulgated to the prefectures, written on silk and sent down.

sentences.zh: 又系囚之具，有枷、杻鉗、鎖，皆有長短廣狹之制，量罪輕重，節級用之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the implements for restraining prisoners included cangues, fetters, manacles, and locks, all having regulations for length, shortness, breadth, and narrowness; according to the lightness or heaviness of the offense, they were applied by graded steps.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the implements for restraining prisoners included cangues, fetters, manacles, and locks, all having regulations for length, shortness, breadth, and narrowness; according to the lightness or heaviness of the offense, they were applied by graded steps.

sentences.zh: 其杖皆削去節目，長三尺五寸。

translations.literal: The staffs all had their nodes shaved off and were three chi five cun in length.
translations.idiomatic: The staffs all had their nodes shaved off and were three chi five cun in length.

sentences.zh: 訊囚杖，大頭徑三分二厘，小頭二分二厘。

translations.literal: The staff for interrogating prisoners had a large end three fen two li in diameter and a small end two fen two li.
translations.idiomatic: The staff for interrogating prisoners had a large end three fen two li in diameter and a small end two fen two li.

sentences.zh: 常行杖，大頭二分七厘，小頭一分七厘。

translations.literal: The staff for regular execution had a large end two fen seven li and a small end one fen seven li.
translations.idiomatic: The staff for regular execution had a large end two fen seven li and a small end one fen seven li.

sentences.zh: 笞杖，大頭二分，小頭一分半。

translations.literal: The rod had a large end two fen and a small end one fen five li.
translations.idiomatic: The rod had a large end two fen and a small end one fen five li.

sentences.zh: 其決笞者，腿分受。

translations.literal: For those receiving rod punishment, the legs received it in divided parts.
translations.idiomatic: For those receiving rod punishment, the legs received it in divided parts.

sentences.zh: 決杖者，背、腿、臀分受。

translations.literal: For those receiving staff punishment, the back, legs, and buttocks received it in divided parts.
translations.idiomatic: For those receiving staff punishment, the back, legs, and buttocks received it in divided parts.

sentences.zh: 及須數等拷訊者，亦同。

translations.literal: For those requiring repeated interrogation by torture, it was likewise the same.
translations.idiomatic: For those requiring repeated interrogation by torture, it was likewise the same.

sentences.zh: 其拷囚不過三度，總數不得過二百。

translations.literal: Torture of prisoners could not exceed three rounds, and the total number could not exceed two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Torture of prisoners could not exceed three rounds, and the total number could not exceed two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 杖罪已下，不得過所犯之數。

translations.literal: For staff offenses and below, it could not exceed the number of the offense committed.
translations.idiomatic: For staff offenses and below, it could not exceed the number prescribed for the offense committed.

sentences.zh: 諸斷罪而無正條，其應出罪者，則舉重以明輕；

translations.literal: In all cases of judging crimes where there was no proper article, for those who should be released from guilt, cite the heavy to clarify the light;
translations.idiomatic: In all cases of judging crimes where there was no proper article, for those who should be released from guilt, cite the heavy to clarify the light;

sentences.zh: 其應入罪者，則舉輕以明重。

translations.literal: for those who should be entered into guilt, cite the light to clarify the heavy.
translations.idiomatic: for those who should be entered into guilt, cite the light to clarify the heavy.

sentences.zh: 稱加者，就重次；

translations.literal: Where it says to add, proceed to the heavier grade;
translations.idiomatic: Where it says to add, proceed to the heavier grade;

sentences.zh: 稱減者，就輕次。

translations.literal: where it says to reduce, proceed to the lighter grade.
translations.idiomatic: where it says to reduce, proceed to the lighter grade.

sentences.zh: 惟二死三流，同為一減，不得加至於死。

translations.literal: Only the two deaths and three exiles together counted as one reduction and could not be added up to death.
translations.idiomatic: Only the two forms of death and the three grades of exile together counted as one reduction and could not be added up to death.

sentences.zh: 斷獄而失於出入者，以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: Those who in judging cases erred in going out or coming in were punished with the crime involved.
translations.idiomatic: Those who in judging cases erred in severity were punished according to the crime involved.

sentences.zh: 失入者，各減三等；

translations.literal: For erroneous severity, each had three grades reduced;
translations.idiomatic: For erroneous severity, each had three grades reduced;

sentences.zh: 失出者，各減五等。

translations.literal: for erroneous leniency, each had five grades reduced.
translations.idiomatic: for erroneous leniency, each had five grades reduced.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以古者斷獄，必訊於三槐九棘之官，乃詔大辟罪，中書、門下五品已上及尚書等議之。

translations.literal: At first, Taizong, because in antiquity judging cases required inquiry before the officials of the Three Pagoda Trees and Nine Thorns, ordained that for great execution crimes, officials of the fifth grade and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery and the Ministers of the Department of State Affairs should deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Taizong, because in antiquity judging cases required inquiry before the officials of the Three Pagoda Trees and Nine Thorns, ordained that for capital offenses, officials of the fifth grade and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery and the Ministers of the Department of State Affairs should deliberate.

sentences.zh: 其後河內人李好德，風疾瞀亂，有妖妄之言，詔按其事。

translations.literal: Thereafter Li Haode of Henei, suffering from wind illness and mental confusion, had deluded and reckless words; an edict ordered investigation of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Li Haode of Henei, suffering from wind illness and mental confusion, uttered deluded and reckless words; an edict ordered investigation of the matter.

sentences.zh: 大理丞張蘊古奏，好德癲病有征，法不當坐。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Yungu memorialized that Haode's epileptic illness had clear signs and that by law he should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Yungu memorialized that Haode's epileptic illness had clear signs and that by law he should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀，劾蘊古貫相州，好德之兄厚德，為其刺史，情在阿縱，奏事不實。

translations.literal: Secretarial Attendant Investigating Censor Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, saying he had passed through Xiangzhou, where Haode's elder brother Houde was its prefect, and that affection led to partial indulgence and that his memorial was not true.
translations.idiomatic: Secretarial Attendant Investigating Censor Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, saying he had passed through Xiangzhou, where Haode's elder brother Houde was its prefect, and that affection led to partial indulgence and that his memorial was untrue.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「吾常禁囚於獄內，蘊古與之弈棋，今復阿縱好德，是亂吾法也。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "We often confined prisoners within the prison; Yungu played chess with them. Now again to indulge Haode partially is to throw Our law into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "We often confined prisoners within the prison; Yungu played chess with them. Now again to indulge Haode partially is to throw Our law into disorder."

sentences.zh: 」遂斬於東市。

translations.literal: He was thereupon executed at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon executed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the Emperor regretted it.

sentences.zh: 又交州都督盧祖尚，以忤旨斬於朝堂，帝亦追悔。

translations.literal: Moreover, Regional Commander of Jiaozhou Lu Zushang was executed in the court hall for defying the imperial will, and the Emperor also later regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Regional Commander of Jiaozhou Lu Zushang was executed in the court hall for defying the imperial will, and the Emperor also later regretted it.

sentences.zh: 下制，凡決死刑，雖令即殺，仍三覆奏。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: for all who were sentenced to death, even when ordered to be killed immediately, there were still three repeated memorials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: for all who were sentenced to death, even when ordered to be killed immediately, there were still three repeated memorials.

sentences.zh: 尋謂侍臣曰：「人命至重，一死不可再生。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he said to his attendant ministers: "Human life is of utmost weight; once dead it cannot be brought back to life."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he said to his attendant ministers: "Human life is of utmost weight; once dead it cannot be brought back to life."

sentences.zh: 昔世充殺鄭頲，既而悔之，追止不及。

translations.literal: In former times Shichong killed Zheng Ting and afterward regretted it, but pursuit to stop it did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Wang Shichong killed Zheng Ting and afterward regretted it, but pursuit to stop it did not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 今春府史取財不多，朕怒殺之，後亦尋悔，皆由思不審也。

translations.literal: This spring a prefectural clerk took not much property; We in anger killed him, and afterward also soon regretted it—all because reflection was not thorough.
translations.idiomatic: This spring a prefectural clerk took not much property; We in anger killed him, and afterward also soon regretted it—all because Our reflection was not thorough.

sentences.zh: 比來決囚，雖三覆奏，須臾之間，三奏便訖，都未得思，三奏何益？

translations.literal: Recently in deciding prisoners, though there were three repeated memorials, within a brief moment the three memorials were finished; there was no time for reflection at all—what use were three memorials?
translations.idiomatic: Recently in deciding prisoners, though there were three repeated memorials, within a brief moment the three memorials were finished; there was no time for reflection at all—what use were three memorials?

sentences.zh: 自今已後，宜二日中五覆奏，下諸州三覆奏。

translations.literal: From now onward, within two days there should be five repeated memorials; sent down to the prefectures, three repeated memorials.
translations.idiomatic: From now onward, within two days there should be five repeated memorials; sent down to the prefectures, three repeated memorials.

sentences.zh: 又古者行刑，君為徹樂減膳。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity when carrying out punishment, the ruler withdrew music and reduced his meals.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in antiquity when carrying out punishment, the ruler withdrew music and reduced his meals.

sentences.zh: 朕今庭無常設之樂，莫知何徹，然對食即不啖酒肉。

translations.literal: We now have no regularly set music in the court hall and do not know what to withdraw, yet when facing a meal We do not eat wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: We now have no regularly set music in the court hall and do not know what to withdraw, yet when facing a meal We do not eat wine or meat.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，令與尚食相知，刑人日勿進酒肉。

translations.literal: From now onward, order the Imperial Commissary to be informed; on days when punishments are carried out, do not present wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: From now onward, order the Imperial Commissary to be informed; on days when punishments are carried out, do not present wine or meat.

sentences.zh: 內教坊及太常，並宜停教。

translations.literal: The Inner Instruction Office and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices should both cease instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Instruction Office and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices should both cease instruction.

sentences.zh: 且曹司斷獄，多據律文，雖情在可矜，而不敢違法，守文定罪，或恐有冤。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the bureaus judged cases they mostly relied on the text of the code; though compassion was warranted in feeling, they did not dare violate the law, adhering to the text to fix guilt—perhaps there were wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the bureaus judged cases they mostly relied on the text of the code; though compassion was warranted in feeling, they did not dare violate the law, adhering to the text to fix guilt—perhaps there were wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 自今門下覆理，有據法合死而情可宥者，宜錄狀奏。

translations.literal: From now the Chancellery should review; where according to law death was warranted but feeling permitted pardon, the circumstances should be recorded and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: From now the Chancellery should review; where according to law death was warranted but feeling permitted pardon, the circumstances should be recorded and memorialized.

sentences.zh: 」自是全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: From this time those fully preserved in life were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From this time those fully preserved in life were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 其五覆奏，以決前一日、二日覆奏，決日又三覆奏。

translations.literal: The five repeated memorials were: one and two days before the decision, repeated memorials; on the day of decision, again three repeated memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The five repeated memorials were: one and two days before the decision, repeated memorials; on the day of decision, again three repeated memorials.

sentences.zh: 惟犯惡逆者，一覆奏而已，著之於令。

translations.literal: Only for those who committed wicked rebellion was one repeated memorial sufficient; this was written into the ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Only for those who committed wicked rebellion was one repeated memorial sufficient; this was written into the ordinances.

sentences.zh: 太宗既誅張蘊古之後，法官以出罪為誡，時有失入者，又不加罪焉，由是刑網頗密。

translations.literal: After Taizong had executed Zhang Yungu, judicial officials took leniency in judgment as a warning; when there were erroneous severity cases, they also did not add punishment—thereby the penal net became rather dense.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong had executed Zhang Yungu, judicial officials took leniency in judgment as a warning; when there were erroneous severity cases, they also did not add punishment—thereby the penal net became rather dense.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問大理卿劉德威曰：「近來刑網稍密，何也？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Director of the Court of Judicial Review Liu Dewei: "Recently the penal net has become somewhat dense—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once asked Director of the Court of Judicial Review Liu Dewei: "Recently the penal net has become somewhat dense—why?"

sentences.zh: 」德威對曰：「律文失入減三等，失出減五等。

translations.literal: Dewei replied: "In the text of the code, erroneous severity reduces three grades; erroneous leniency reduces five grades."
translations.idiomatic: Dewei replied: "In the text of the code, erroneous severity reduces three grades; erroneous leniency reduces five grades."

sentences.zh: 今失入則無辜，失出則便獲大罪，所由吏皆深文。

translations.literal: Now if there is erroneous severity there is no guilt, but if there is erroneous leniency one immediately receives a great crime—the clerks responsible all apply the law harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Now if there is erroneous severity there is no guilt, but if there is erroneous leniency one immediately receives a great punishment—the clerks responsible all apply the law harshly.

sentences.zh: 」太宗然其言。

translations.literal: Taizong approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved his words.

sentences.zh: 由是失於出入者，令依律文，斷獄者漸為平允。

translations.literal: Thereby for errors in going out or coming in, they were ordered to follow the text of the code, and those judging cases gradually became fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby for errors in severity, they were ordered to follow the text of the code, and those judging cases gradually became fair and even.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又制流罪三等，不限以里數，量配邊惡之州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, they also ordained three grades of exile offenses, not limited by li distance, but assigned according to measure to border regions and harsh prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, they also ordained three grades of exile offenses, not limited by li distance, but assigned according to measure to border regions and harsh prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其後雖存寬典，而犯者漸少。

translations.literal: Thereafter, though lenient canons remained, offenders gradually became fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, though lenient canons remained, offenders gradually became fewer.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遵貞觀故事，務在恤刑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he followed the precedents of Zhenguan and strove to show compassion in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he followed the precedents of Zhenguan and strove to show compassion in punishment.

sentences.zh: 嘗問大理卿唐臨在獄系囚之數，臨對曰：「見囚五十餘人，惟二人合死。

translations.literal: He once asked Director of the Court of Judicial Review Tang Lin the number of prisoners detained in the prisons; Lin replied: "The prisoners presently seen are more than fifty persons; only two warrant death."
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Director of the Court of Judicial Review Tang Lin the number of prisoners detained in the prisons; Lin replied: "The prisoners presently seen are more than fifty persons; only two warrant death."

sentences.zh: 」帝以囚數全少，怡然形於顏色。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the number of prisoners was entirely few, showed ease in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, because the number of prisoners was entirely few, showed ease in his countenance.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，敕太尉長孫無忌、司空李勣、左僕射于志寧、右僕射行成、侍中高季輔、黃門侍郎宇文節柳奭、右丞段寶玄、太常少卿令狐德棻、吏部侍郎高敬言、刑部侍郎劉燕客、給事中趙文恪，中書舍人李友益、少府丞張行實、大理丞元紹、太府丞王文端、刑部郎中賈敏行等，共撰定律令格式。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yonghui, he commanded Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Right Vice Director Xing Cheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Jifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuwen Jie and Liu Shi, Right Assistant Director Duan Baoxuan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Linghu Defen, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Jingyan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yanke, Attendant within the Yellow Gate Zhao Wenke, Secretariat Drafter Li Youyi, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories Zhang Xingshi, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Shao, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Wang Wenduan, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Justice Jia Minxing, and others jointly to compile and fix laws, ordinances, regulations, and forms.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning of Yonghui, he commanded Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Right Vice Director Xing Cheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Jifu, Vice Directors of the Secretariat Yuwen Jie and Liu Shi, Right Assistant Director Duan Baoxuan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Linghu Defen, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Jingyan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yanke, Attendant within the Yellow Gate Zhao Wenke, Secretariat drafter Li Youyi, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories Zhang Xingshi, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Shao, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Wang Wenduan, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Justice Jia Minxing, and others jointly to compile laws, ordinances, regulations, and forms.

sentences.zh: 舊制不便者，皆隨刪改。

translations.literal: Old institutions that were inconvenient were all revised and changed as they went.
translations.idiomatic: Old institutions that were inconvenient were all revised and changed as they went.

sentences.zh: 遂分格為兩部：曹司常務為《留司格》，天下所共者為《散頒格》。

translations.literal: They then divided the regulations into two parts: standing duties of the bureaus became the Retained Bureau Regulations; what was shared throughout the realm became the Broadly Promulgated Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: They then divided the regulations into two parts: standing duties of the bureaus became the Retained Bureau Regulations; what was shared throughout the realm became the Broadly Promulgated Regulations.

sentences.zh: 其《散頒格》下州縣，《留司格》但留本司行用焉。

translations.literal: The Broadly Promulgated Regulations were sent down to prefectures and counties; the Retained Bureau Regulations were kept only by the original bureaus for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Broadly Promulgated Regulations were sent down to prefectures and counties; the Retained Bureau Regulations were kept only by the original bureaus for implementation.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「律學未有定疏，每年所舉明法，遂無憑准。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict said: "Legal studies have no fixed commentary; each year those recommended for mastery of law thus have no standard to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict said: "Legal studies have no fixed commentary; each year those recommended for mastery of law thus have no standard to rely on."

sentences.zh: 宜廣召解律人條義疏奏聞。

translations.literal: It is fitting broadly to summon those who understand law to set forth the articles in commentary and memorialize for report.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting broadly to summon those who understand law to set forth the articles in commentary and memorialize for report.

sentences.zh: 仍使中書、門下監定。

translations.literal: They should also have the Secretariat and Chancellery supervise and fix it.
translations.idiomatic: They should also have the Secretariat and Chancellery supervise and fix it.

sentences.zh: 」於是太尉趙國公無忌、司空英國公勣、尚書左僕射兼太子少師監修國史燕國公志寧、銀青光祿大夫刑部尚書唐臨、太中大夫守大理卿段寶玄、朝議大夫守尚書右丞劉燕客、朝議大夫守御史中丞賈敏行等，參撰《律疏》，成三十卷，四年十月奏之，頒於天下。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. Thereupon Grand Preceptor, Duke of Zhao, Wuji; Minister of Works, Duke of Ying, Ji; Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History, Duke of Yan, Zhining; Tang Lin, Minister of Justice with the silver-green-gold glory rank; Duan Baoxuan, Acting Grand Justice of the Court of Judicial Review with the Grand Master rank; Liu Yanke, Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with the Court Gentleman for Consultation rank; Jia Minxing, Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief with the Court Gentleman for Consultation rank, and others jointly compiled the Code Commentary, completing thirty juan. In the tenth month of the fourth year they memorialized it and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Duke of Zhao; Minister of Works Li Ji, Duke of Ying; Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Duke of Yan, who also served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and supervisor of the national history; Tang Lin, Minister of Justice; Duan Baoxuan, Acting Grand Justice; Liu Yanke, Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Jia Minxing, Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief; and others jointly compiled the Code Commentary in thirty juan. In the tenth month of the fourth year they submitted it to the throne and promulgated it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自是斷獄者皆引疏分析之。

translations.literal: From this time onward, those who decided cases all cited the commentary in analyzing them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all who tried cases cited the Code Commentary in their analysis.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年五月，上謂侍臣曰：「獄訟繁多，皆由刑罰枉濫，故曰刑者成也，一成而不可變。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "Cases and lawsuits are numerous, all because punishments are applied in error and excess. Therefore it is said: punishment means completion—once completed, it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "Lawsuits are numerous, all because punishments are wrongly and excessively applied. As the saying goes, punishment means completion—once fixed, it must not be changed.

sentences.zh: 末代斷獄之人，皆以苛刻為明，是以秦氏網密秋荼，而獲罪者眾。

translations.literal: Those who decided cases in the final ages all regarded harshness as clarity. Thus the Qin family's net was tight as autumn's bitter tea, and those who incurred guilt were many.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates in declining ages all took harshness for wisdom. That is why the Qin regime cast so tight a net—dense as autumn's bitter tea—and so many were found guilty.

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，四海乂安，欲與公等共行寬政。

translations.literal: Today the realm is without trouble and the four seas are governed in peace. I wish to practice lenient governance together with you.
