translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and the four seas are tranquil. I wish to pursue lenient government together with you.

sentences.zh: 今日刑罰，得無枉濫乎？

translations.literal: Today's punishments—might they not be applied in error and excess?
translations.idiomatic: Are punishments today not still being wrongly and excessively applied?

sentences.zh: 」無忌對曰：「陛下欲得刑法寬平，臣下猶不識聖意。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. Wuji replied: "Your Majesty wishes to obtain leniency and fairness in criminal law, yet your officials still do not understand the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji replied: "Your Majesty wishes the criminal code to be lenient and fair, yet your officials still fail to grasp your intent.

sentences.zh: 此法弊來已久，非止今日。

translations.literal: The abuses of this law have come from long ago—not only today.
translations.idiomatic: These abuses in the law have persisted for a long time; they did not begin only today.

sentences.zh: 若情在體國，即共號癡人，意在深文，便稱好吏。

translations.literal: If one's feeling lies in cherishing the state, they are together styled fools; if one's intent lies in severe wording of charges, one is called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: If one truly cares for the welfare of the state, everyone calls him a fool; if one aims to word charges as severely as possible, he is praised as an excellent official.

sentences.zh: 所以罪雖合杖，必欲遣徒，理有可生，務入於死，非憎前人，陷於死刑。

translations.literal: Thus though guilt fit flogging, one must have them sent to penal servitude; though reason allowed life, one strives to bring them to death—not from hatred of the person, but to entrap them in capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, even when guilt warranted only flogging, officials insist on penal servitude; even when the case reasonably allowed life, they strive to secure a death sentence—not because they hate the accused, but because they wish to trap him in a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜而令放，法司亦宜固請，但陛下喜怒不妄加於人，刑罰自然適中。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty shows pity and orders release, the judicial offices should also firmly petition accordingly. But if Your Majesty does not capriciously add favor or anger toward people, punishments will naturally be balanced.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty shows mercy and orders release, the judicial offices ought to petition firmly in support. But if Your Majesty does not capriciously visit favor or anger upon people, punishments will naturally fall into proper balance.

sentences.zh: 」上以為然。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. The emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年七月，上謂侍臣曰：「律通比附，條例太多。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "The code widely uses analogical application, and there are too many articles and examples.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "The code relies too heavily on analogical application, and there are far too many articles and precedents.

sentences.zh: 」左僕射志寧等對：「舊律多比附斷事，乃稍難解。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. Left Vice Director Zhining and others replied: "The old code often decided cases by analogical application, and was thus somewhat difficult to understand.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yu Zhining and others replied: "The old code decided many cases by analogical application, which made it somewhat hard to understand.

sentences.zh: 科條極眾，數至三千。

translations.literal: Statutory provisions were extremely numerous, reaching as many as three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The statutory provisions were extremely numerous, numbering as many as three thousand.

sentences.zh: 隋日再定，惟留五百。

translations.literal: In the Sui day it was re-fixed twice, and only five hundred were retained.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it was revised twice, leaving only five hundred provisions.

sentences.zh: 以事類相似者，比附科斷。

translations.literal: Cases of similar type were judged by analogical application of statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Cases of similar type were decided by applying analogous statutes.

sentences.zh: 今日所停，即是參取隋律修易。

translations.literal: What has now been set aside is precisely what was revised and simplified with reference to the Sui code.
translations.idiomatic: What has now been discontinued is precisely the material that was revised and simplified with reference to the Sui code.

sentences.zh: 條章既少，極成省便。

translations.literal: Since the articles and chapters are fewer, they are extremely convenient and economical.
translations.idiomatic: With fewer articles and chapters, the code is greatly simplified and easier to use.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改易官號，因敕司刑太常伯源直心、少常伯李敬玄、司刑大夫李文禮等重定格式，惟改曹局之名，而不易篇第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, official titles were changed. An edict therefore ordered Yuan Zhixin, Grand Minister of Criminal Affairs; Li Jingxuan, Junior Minister; Li Wenli, Senior Commissioner of Criminal Affairs, and others to re-fix the statutes and forms, changing only the names of offices and bureaus but not altering the chapters and sections.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo, official titles were changed. By edict, Yuan Zhixin, Grand Minister of Criminal Affairs; Li Jingxuan, Junior Minister; Li Wenli, Senior Commissioner of Criminal Affairs; and others were ordered to revise the statutes and forms, changing only bureau names while leaving the chapters and sections unchanged.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年奏上。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde it was memorialized and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: It was submitted to the throne in the second year of Linde.

sentences.zh: 至儀鳳中，官號復舊，又敕左僕射劉仁軌、右僕射戴至德、侍中張文瓘、中書令李敬玄、右庶子郝處俊、黃門侍郎來恆、左庶子高智周、右庶子李義琰、吏部侍郎裴行儉馬載、兵部侍郎蕭德昭裴炎、工部侍郎李義琛、刑部侍郎張楚、金部郎中盧律師等，刪緝格式。

translations.literal: By the Yifeng era, official titles were restored to the old form. Another edict ordered Left Vice Director Liu Rengui, Right Vice Director Dai Zhide, Palace Attendant Zhang Wenjin, Grand Secretary Li Jingxuan, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Hao Chujun, Huangmen Vice Director Lai Heng, Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Gao Zhizhou, Right Vice Director Li Yiyan, Vice Directors of the Ministry of Personnel Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai, Vice Directors of the Ministry of War Xiao Dezhao and Pei Yan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Li Yichen, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Zhang Chu, Jinbu Bureau Director Lu Lushi, and others to prune and compile the statutes and forms.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yifeng era, official titles had been restored. Another edict ordered Left Vice Director Liu Rengui, Right Vice Director Dai Zhide, Palace Attendant Zhang Wenjin, Grand Secretary Li Jingxuan, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Hao Chujun, Huangmen Vice Director Lai Heng, Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Gao Zhizhou, Right Vice Director Li Yiyan, Vice Directors of Personnel Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai, Vice Directors of War Xiao Dezhao and Pei Yan, Vice Director of Works Li Yichen, Vice Director of Justice Zhang Chu, Jinbu Bureau Director Lu Lushi, and others to revise and compile the statutes and forms.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年二月九日，撰定奏上。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the second month of the second year of Yifeng, compilation was completed and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the second month of the second year of Yifeng, the revised compilation was submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先是詳刑少卿趙仁本撰《法例》三卷，引以斷獄，時議亦為折衷。

translations.literal: Previously, Vice Minister of Detailed Punishment Zhao Renben compiled three juan of Legal Precedents, which were cited in trying cases; contemporaries also regarded them as a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Minister of Detailed Punishment Zhao Renben had compiled three juan of Legal Precedents, which were cited in deciding cases and were widely regarded as a reasonable compromise.

sentences.zh: 後高宗覽之，以為煩文不便。

translations.literal: Later Gaozong reviewed them and considered the verbose text inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gaozong reviewed them, he found the verbose text impractical.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「律、令、格、式，天下通規，非朕庸虛所能創制。

translations.literal: He therefore said to his attendant ministers: "Codes, ordinances, regulations, and forms are universal regulations of the realm—not something that I, empty and mediocre, could create.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore said to his attendant ministers: "Codes, ordinances, regulations, and forms are the universal standards of the realm—not something that I, unworthy as I am, could have created on my own.

sentences.zh: 並是武德之際，貞觀已來，或取定宸衷，參詳眾議，條章備舉，軌躅昭然，臨事遵行，自不能盡。

translations.literal: All were from the Wude period and since the Zhenguan era—sometimes fixed in the imperial heart, sometimes deliberated with the multitude of counsels. Articles and chapters were fully set forth, tracks and footprints clearly displayed; in handling affairs one could not fully follow them even when one tried.
translations.idiomatic: All of them date from the Wude period and the Zhenguan era onward—sometimes fixed by imperial decision, sometimes worked out through broad consultation. Their articles are complete and their standards clear, yet even when one tries to follow them in practice, one cannot do so fully.

sentences.zh: 何為更須作例，致使觸緒多疑。

translations.literal: Why must one additionally make precedents, causing one to touch upon many doubts when following threads?
translations.idiomatic: Why must we add further precedents, only to create endless doubt whenever a case is examined?

sentences.zh: 計此因循，非適今日，速宜改轍，不得更然。

translations.literal: This practice of perpetuating the old has not been limited to today. It should quickly change course and not be allowed to continue.
translations.idiomatic: This habit of clinging to old ways is nothing new. The course should be changed at once and not allowed to continue.

sentences.zh: 」自是，《法例》遂廢不用。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. From then on, the Legal Precedents were abandoned and no longer used.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, the Legal Precedents were abandoned and no longer used.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，初欲大收人望。

translations.literal: When Zetian assumed the regency, at first she wished greatly to win popular regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian assumed the regency, she at first wished greatly to win popular support.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初年，令熔銅為匭，四面置門，各依方色，共為一室。

translations.literal: In the early years of Chuigong, she ordered copper melted to make boxes, with gates set on four sides according to the colors of the four directions, all together forming one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chuigong period, she ordered copper cast into boxes with gates on all four sides, each colored according to its direction, together forming one chamber.

sentences.zh: 東面名曰延恩匭，上賦頌及許求官爵者封表投之。

translations.literal: The eastern side was called the Extended Favor Box; those submitting panegyrics and those petitioning for offices and ranks put sealed memorials into it.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern side was called the Extended Favor Box; those submitting encomia and those petitioning for office and rank deposited sealed memorials there.

sentences.zh: 南面曰招諫匭，有言時政得失及直言諫諍者投之。

translations.literal: The southern side was called the Recruitment of Remonstrance Box; those with words on the gains and losses of current policy and those offering direct remonstrance put them in.
translations.idiomatic: The southern side was called the Recruitment of Remonstrance Box; those commenting on the merits and failings of current policy or offering blunt remonstrance deposited their submissions there.

sentences.zh: 西面曰申冤匭，有得罪冤濫者投之。

translations.literal: The western side was called the Petition for Wronged Innocence Box; those who had suffered unjust conviction put them in.
translations.idiomatic: The western side was called the Petition for Wronged Innocence Box; those who had been wrongfully convicted deposited their petitions there.

sentences.zh: 北面曰通玄匭，有玄象災變及軍謀秘策者投之。

translations.literal: The northern side was called the Communication of Mysteries Box; those with omens, disasters, and secret military stratagems put them in.
translations.idiomatic: The northern side was called the Communication of Mysteries Box; those reporting celestial omens, disasters, or secret military plans deposited their submissions there.

sentences.zh: 每日置之於朝堂，以收天下表疏。

translations.literal: Each day they were placed in the court hall to receive memorials from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Each day the boxes were placed in the court hall to receive memorials from throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 既出之後，不逞之徒，或至攻訐陰私，謗訕朝政者。

translations.literal: After they were put out, unscrupulous persons sometimes went so far as to attack others' private affairs and slander current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Once the boxes were opened to the public, unscrupulous people sometimes used them to attack others' private affairs or slander the government.

sentences.zh: 後乃令中書、門下官一人，專監其所投之狀，仍責識官，然後許進封，行之至今焉。

translations.literal: Later it was ordered that one official each from the Secretariat and Chancellery should specially supervise the petitions submitted, and that officials must endorse them before sealed submission was permitted—a practice continuing to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Later, one official each from the Secretariat and Chancellery was assigned to supervise the submissions, and an endorsing official was required before a sealed petition could be accepted—a practice that continues to the present.

sentences.zh: 則天又敕內史裴居道、夏官尚書岑長倩、鳳閣侍郎韋方質與刪定官袁智弘等十餘人，刪改格式，加計帳及勾帳式，通舊式成二十卷。

translations.literal: Zetian also ordered Imperial Secretary Pei Judao, Minister of Summer Offices Cen Changqian, Fengge Vice Director Wei Fangzhi, and more than ten revising officials including Yuan Zhihong to revise the statutes and forms, adding accounting and audit forms, making twenty juan in all together with the old forms.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian also ordered Imperial Secretary Pei Judao, Minister of Summer Offices Cen Changqian, Fengge Vice Director Wei Fangzhi, and more than ten revising officials including Yuan Zhihong to revise the statutes and forms, adding accounting and audit forms, for a total of twenty juan together with the old forms.

sentences.zh: 又以武德已來、垂拱已前詔敕便於時者，編為《新格》二卷，則天自製序。

translations.literal: She also compiled timely edicts and orders from Wude onward through before Chuigong into two juan of the New Regulations, with a preface written by Zetian herself.
translations.idiomatic: She also compiled edicts and orders from Wude down to before Chuigong that remained useful into two juan of the New Regulations, for which Wu Zetian herself wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 其二卷之外，別編六卷，堪為當司行用，為《垂拱留司格》。

translations.literal: Apart from these two juan, six additional juan were separately compiled as usable by the departments concerned, titled the Chuigong Retained-Office Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond those two juan, six additional juan were separately compiled for use by the relevant departments, titled the Chuigong Retained-Office Regulations.

sentences.zh: 時韋方質詳練法理，又委其事于咸陽尉王守慎，又有經理之才，故《垂拱格》、《式》，議者稱為詳密。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Fangzhi was thoroughly versed in legal principles, and the task was also entrusted to Xianyang Prefect Wang Shoushen, who likewise had talent for managing affairs. Therefore the Chuigong Regulations and Forms were praised by commentators as detailed and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Fangzhi was thoroughly versed in legal doctrine, and the work was also entrusted to Xianyang Prefect Wang Shoushen, who had a gift for administration. Commentators therefore praised the Chuigong Regulations and Forms as detailed and thorough.

sentences.zh: 其律令惟改二十四條，又有不便者，大抵依舊。

translations.literal: Of the code and ordinances, only twenty-four articles were changed; where there were inconvenient points, for the most part the old provisions were kept.
translations.idiomatic: Of the code and ordinances, only twenty-four articles were changed; where revision would have been inconvenient, the old provisions were largely retained.

sentences.zh: 然則天嚴于用刑，屬徐敬業作亂，及豫、博兵起之後，恐人心動搖，欲以威制天下，漸引酷吏，務令深文，以案刑獄。

translations.literal: Yet Zetian was strict in employing punishments. When Xu Jingye raised rebellion and after troops rose in Yu and Bo, fearing that hearts would waver, she wished to control the realm by severity and gradually employed harsh officials, striving for severe wording in cases to try criminal prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu Zetian was severe in the use of punishment. After Xu Jingye's rebellion and the uprisings in Yu and Bo, fearing that hearts would waver, she sought to control the realm through terror and gradually brought in harsh officials, insisting on severe wording of charges to prosecute criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 長壽年有上封事言嶺表流人有陰謀逆者，乃遣司刑評事萬國俊攝監察御史就案之，若得反狀，斬決。

translations.literal: In the Changshou era a sealed memorial stated that among exiles in Lingnan there were those plotting treason in secret. Thereupon Acting Censor Wan Guojun was dispatched as Acting Investigating Censor to examine the matter; if evidence of rebellion was obtained, they were to be executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changshou era a sealed memorial reported that exiles in Lingnan were secretly plotting rebellion. Wan Guojun, a judicial reviewer acting as investigating censor, was dispatched to investigate; anyone for whom evidence of rebellion could be obtained was to be executed.

sentences.zh: 國俊至廣州，遍召流人，擁之水曲，以次加戮。

translations.literal: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles, gathered them at a bend of the water, and executed them one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all the exiles, gathered them at a bend in the river, and executed them one after another.

sentences.zh: 三百餘人，一時並命，然後鍛煉曲成反狀。

translations.literal: More than three hundred people were killed at once; only afterward were confessions of rebellion forged and twisted into shape.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred people were killed at once; only afterward were confessions of rebellion forged and twisted into shape.

sentences.zh: 乃更誣奏云：「諸道流人，多有怨望。

translations.literal: He then further submitted a false memorial saying: "Exiles in the various circuits mostly harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a false memorial saying: "Exiles in the various circuits mostly harbor resentment.

sentences.zh: 若不推究，為變不遙。

translations.literal: If not thoroughly investigated, rebellion will not be far off.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not thoroughly investigated, rebellion will not be far off.

sentences.zh: 」則天深然其言。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. Zetian deeply agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 又命攝監察御史劉光業、王德壽、鮑思恭、王處貞、屈貞筠等，分往劍南、黔中、安南、嶺南等六道，按鞫流人。

translations.literal: She further ordered Acting Censors Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and others to go separately to the six circuits of Jiannan, Qianzhong, Annam, Lingnan, and others to investigate and interrogate exiles.
translations.idiomatic: She further ordered Acting Censors Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and others to go separately to the six circuits of Jiannan, Qianzhong, Annam, Lingnan, and elsewhere to investigate and interrogate exiles.

sentences.zh: 光業所在殺戮。

translations.literal: Where Guangye went, slaughter ensued.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Liu Guangye went, slaughter followed.

sentences.zh: 光業誅九百人，德壽誅七百人，其餘少者不減數百人。

translations.literal: Guangye killed nine hundred men; Deshou killed seven hundred; the others killed no fewer than several hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye executed nine hundred people, Deshou seven hundred, and the others no fewer than several hundred each.

sentences.zh: 亦有雜犯及遠年流人，亦枉及禍焉。

translations.literal: There were also miscellaneous offenders and exiles from distant years who were wrongly swept into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous offenders and exiles from years long past were also wrongly swept up in the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 時周興、來俊臣等，相次受制推究大獄。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were successively commanded to investigate major cases.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were successively ordered to investigate major cases.

sentences.zh: 乃于都城麗景門內，別置推事使院，時人謂之「新開獄」。

translations.literal: A separate Office of Interrogation Commissioners was set up inside Lijing Gate in the capital, which people of the time called the "Newly Opened Prison."
translations.idiomatic: A separate Office of Interrogation Commissioners was established inside Lijing Gate in the capital, which people of the time called the "Newly Opened Prison."

sentences.zh: 俊臣又與侍御史侯思止王弘義郭霸李敬仁、評事康暐衛遂忠等，招集告事數百人，共為羅織，以陷良善。

translations.literal: Junchen also together with Attending Censor Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Ba, Li Jingren, Reviewer Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others gathered several hundred informants to weave false charges together and entrap the good.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen also joined Attending Censors Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Ba, and Li Jingren, Reviewers Kang Wei and Wei Suizhong, and others in gathering several hundred informants to weave false charges and entrap the innocent.

sentences.zh: 前後枉遭殺害者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Those wrongfully killed before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The number of people wrongfully killed in this way was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 又造《告密羅織經》一卷，其意旨皆網羅前人，織成反狀。

translations.literal: He also produced one juan of the Classic of Secret Accusation and Fabricated Charges, its import being entirely to ensnare people and weave charges of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled one juan of the Classic of Secret Accusation and Fabricated Charges, whose whole purpose was to ensnare people and fabricate charges of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 俊臣每鞫囚，無問輕重，多以醋灌鼻。

translations.literal: Whenever Junchen interrogated prisoners, regardless of severity, he often poured vinegar into their noses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Junchen interrogated prisoners, regardless of the severity of the charge, he often poured vinegar into their noses.

sentences.zh: 禁地牢中，或盛之於甕，以火圍繞炙之。

translations.literal: In secret dungeons, some were placed in jars with fire circling around to roast them.
translations.idiomatic: In secret dungeons, some were placed in jars with fire built around them to roast them alive.

sentences.zh: 兼絕其糧餉，至有抽衣絮以啖之者。

translations.literal: He also cut off their food rations, so that some tore out the cotton from their clothes to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut off their food, so that some tore the cotton padding from their clothes to eat.

sentences.zh: 其所作大枷，凡有十號：一曰定百脈，二曰喘不得，三曰突地吼，四曰著即承，五曰失魂膽，六曰實同反，七曰反是實，八曰死豬愁，九曰求即死，十曰求破家。

translations.literal: The great cangues he made numbered ten in all: first, Fixes the Hundred Pulses; second, Cannot Breathe; third, Earth-Shaking Roar; fourth, Put On and Confess at Once; fifth, Loss of Soul and Gall; sixth, Truth Same as Rebellion; seventh, Rebellion Is the Truth; eighth, Dead Pig's Sorrow; ninth, Seek and Die at Once; tenth, Seek and Destroy the Family.
translations.idiomatic: The great cangues he devised numbered ten in all: Fixes the Hundred Pulses, Cannot Breathe, Earth-Shaking Roar, Put On and Confess at Once, Loss of Soul and Gall, Truth Same as Rebellion, Rebellion Is the Truth, Dead Pig's Sorrow, Seek and Die at Once, and Seek and Destroy the Family.

sentences.zh: 又令寢處糞穢，備諸苦毒。

translations.literal: He also made them sleep amid filth and ordure, providing every kind of bitter poison.
translations.idiomatic: He also made them sleep amid filth and ordure, subjecting them to every kind of torment.

sentences.zh: 每有制書寬宥囚徒，俊臣必先遣獄卒，盡殺重罪，然後宣示。

translations.literal: Whenever an imperial edict granted leniency to prisoners, Junchen would first send jailers to kill all those guilty of serious crimes, and only then announce the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an imperial edict granted leniency to prisoners, Junchen would first send jailers to kill all those charged with serious crimes, and only then announce the edict.

sentences.zh: 是時海內懾懼，道路以目。

translations.literal: At that time the realm within the seas was gripped by fear; people on the roads met one another's eyes only with dread.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the whole realm lived in terror; people on the roads dared only to glance at one another.

sentences.zh: 麟台正字陳子昂上書曰：

translations.literal: Chen Ziao, Rectifier of the Office of Archive, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziao, Rectifier of the Office of the Archive, submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之禦天下者，其政有三：王者化之，用仁義也；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those who governed the realm in antiquity had three kinds of governance: kings transformed it, using benevolence and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who governed the realm in antiquity pursued three kinds of policy: kings transformed the people through benevolence and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 霸者威之，任權智也；

translations.literal: hegemons awed it, relying on authority and cunning;
translations.idiomatic: hegemons awed them through authority and cunning;

sentences.zh: 強國脅之，務刑罰也。

translations.literal: strong states coerced it, devoting themselves to punishments.
translations.idiomatic: strong states coerced them through punishments alone.

sentences.zh: 是以化之不足，然後威之，威之不足，然後刑之。

translations.literal: Thus when transformation was insufficient, they then awed; when awe was insufficient, they then punished.
translations.idiomatic: When transformation proved insufficient, they turned to awe; when awe proved insufficient, they turned to punishment.

sentences.zh: 故至於刑，則非王者之所貴矣。

translations.literal: Therefore when it came to punishment, that was not what kings prized.
translations.idiomatic: Thus punishment was never what true kings valued most.

sentences.zh: 況欲光宅天下，追功上皇，專任刑殺以為威斷，可謂策之失者也。

translations.literal: How much the more, when one wishes to spread light throughout the realm and pursue merit surpassing the former sovereign, yet relies exclusively on killing as awe and judgment—it may be called a failure of policy.
translations.idiomatic: How much less should one who wishes to illuminate the realm and surpass the achievements of the former sovereign rely exclusively on killing as a means of imposing authority—surely this is a mistaken policy.

sentences.zh: 臣伏睹陛下聖德聰明，遊心太古，將制靜宇宙，保乂黎民，發號施令，出於誠慊。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly observes that Your Majesty's sage virtue is wise and bright, your heart roams in deepest antiquity. You will pacify the cosmos and preserve the people, issuing commands from sincere sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that Your Majesty is sage and wise, your heart set on the ideals of deepest antiquity, intent on pacifying the universe and preserving the people, issuing commands from genuine sincerity.

sentences.zh: 天下蒼生，莫不懸望聖風，冀見神化，道德為政，將侍于陛下矣。

translations.literal: The common people of the realm all look up in hope for the sage wind, longing to see divine transformation—moral governance is about to attend upon Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the realm all look up in hope for your sage influence, longing to witness true transformation; moral government is about to rest with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，聖人出，必有驅除，蓋天人之符，應休命也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when a sage appears, there must be driving out—surely a sign between Heaven and man, responding to a glorious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a sage ruler appears, wrongdoers must be driven out—surely a sign of accord between Heaven and man, answering a glorious mandate.

sentences.zh: 日者東南微孽，敢謀亂常。

translations.literal: Recently a petty evil in the southeast dared to plot disorder against the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a petty rebel force in the southeast dared to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陛下順天行誅，罪惡咸伏，豈非天意欲彰陛下威武之功哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty followed Heaven in carrying out punishment; all wickedness submitted. Is this not Heaven's intent to display Your Majesty's martial awe and merit!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty followed Heaven in carrying out punishment, and all wickedness was subdued—is this not Heaven's intent to display your martial glory!

sentences.zh: 而執事者不察天心，以為人意，惡其首亂唱禍，法合誅屠，將息奸源，窮其黨與。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge did not discern Heaven's heart and took it as human intent. Hating those who first stirred disorder and raised calamity, they considered the law to warrant execution, wishing to extinguish the source of treachery and exhaust their associates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those in charge failed to discern Heaven's intent and treated it as mere human zeal. Hating those who first stirred rebellion and spread calamity, they held that the law required execution, wishing to cut off the source of treachery and exhaust their associates.

sentences.zh: 遂使陛下大開詔獄，重設嚴刑，冀以懲奸，觀於天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon they caused Your Majesty to greatly open the edict prison and heavily establish severe punishments, hoping thereby to punish treachery and be observed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore caused Your Majesty to open the edict prison on a vast scale and impose severe punishments anew, hoping thereby to punish treachery and make an example before the realm.

sentences.zh: 逆党親屬及其交遊，有涉嫌疑，辭相連及，莫不窮捕考校，枝葉蟠拿。

translations.literal: Relatives of rebel factions and their associates—wherever suspicion was involved, testimonies linked one to another—all were pursued to the limit, captured, and examined; branches and leaves were entangled and seized.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives of the rebels and their associates—wherever suspicion attached, testimony linked one case to another—all were hunted down, arrested, and interrogated without limit; branches and leaves were entangled and seized together.

sentences.zh: 大或流血，小禦魑魅。

translations.literal: The great sometimes shed blood; the small were used to drive off evil spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Great offenders sometimes shed blood; even petty suspects were pursued as if to drive off demons.

sentences.zh: 至有奸人熒惑，乘險相誣，糾告疑似，冀圖爵賞，叫于闕下者，日有數矣。

translations.literal: So much so that wicked men, deluding others, took advantage of danger to accuse one another, lodging reports on mere suspicion in hope of rank and reward. Those crying out below the palace gates numbered several each day.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men even took advantage of the turmoil to delude and accuse one another, lodging reports on mere suspicion in hope of rank and reward; several such cries were heard below the palace gates each day.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷徨徨，莫能自固，海內傾聽，以相驚恐。

translations.literal: At that time the court was restless and unable to steady itself; the realm within the seas listened anxiously, fright spreading among all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was unsettled and could not steady itself; the whole realm listened in anxiety, and fear spread among all.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下仁慈，憫其危懼，賜以恩詔，許其大功已上，一切勿論。

translations.literal: Thanks to Your Majesty's benevolence, pitying their terror, you granted a gracious edict permitting that for those reaching the level of dagong and above, all should not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's benevolence, pitying their terror, you issued a gracious edict permitting that even the gravest offenses would go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 人時獲泰，謂生再造。

translations.literal: People at the time obtained peace and considered it a second birth.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time found relief and spoke of being given life anew.

sentences.zh: 愚臣竊以忻然，賀陛下聖明，得天之機也。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant privately rejoiced, congratulating Your Majesty on your sage clarity in seizing Heaven's opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: I privately rejoiced, congratulating Your Majesty on your sage clarity in seizing Heaven's timely opportunity.

sentences.zh: 不謂議者異見，又執前圖，比者刑獄，紛紛復起。

translations.literal: I did not expect that counsellors with divergent views would again cling to the former course; recently criminal prisons have repeatedly flared up.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that counsellors with other views would again cling to the former course; recently criminal prosecutions have repeatedly flared up.

sentences.zh: 陛下不深思天意，以順休期，尚以督察為理，威刑為務，使前者之詔，不信於人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not deeply ponder Heaven's intent to follow this glorious era, yet still takes supervision as governance and awe through punishment as the task, causing the earlier edict not to be trusted by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not deeply ponder Heaven's intent so as to follow this auspicious age, yet still takes supervision as governance and terror through punishment as the chief task, so that your earlier edict is no longer trusted by the people.

sentences.zh: 愚臣昧焉，竊恐非五帝、三王伐罪吊人之意也。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant is obscure, but I privately fear this is not the intent of the Five Emperors and Three Kings in punishing crime and comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: I am but a foolish servant, yet I privately fear this is not what the Five Emperors and Three Kings intended when they punished the guilty and comforted the people.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀當今天下百姓，思安久矣。

translations.literal: Your servant privately observes that the common people of the realm today have long yearned for peace.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the people of the realm today have long yearned for peace.

sentences.zh: 曩屬北胡侵塞，西戎寇邊，兵革相屠，向曆十載。

translations.literal: Formerly they suffered northern barbarians invading the frontier and western Rong raiding the borders; weapons and armor mutually slaughtered for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly they suffered northern barbarians invading the frontier and western tribes raiding the borders; armies slaughtered one another for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 關、河自北，轉輸幽、燕；

translations.literal: From Pass and River northward, transport was dispatched to You and Yan;
translations.idiomatic: From the passes and rivers of the north, supplies were transported to You and Yan;

sentences.zh: 秦、蜀之西，馳騖湟、海。

translations.literal: West of Qin and Shu, horses galloped toward Huang and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: west of Qin and Shu, armies galloped toward Huangzhong and the western sea.

sentences.zh: 當時天下疲極矣！

translations.literal: At that time the realm was utterly exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was utterly exhausted!

sentences.zh: 重以大兵之後，屬遭凶年，流離饑餓，死喪略半。

translations.literal: Compounded by great campaigns afterward, they then suffered famine years; displaced, starving, the dead were nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Compounding the burden of great campaigns, famine years followed; people were displaced and starving, and nearly half the population died.

sentences.zh: 幸賴陛下以至聖之德，撫寧兆人，邊境獲安，中國無事，陰陽大順，年穀累登，天下父子，始得相養矣。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on Your Majesty's most sage virtue to soothe and settle the myriad people, the frontiers obtained peace, the central domains were untroubled, yin and yang greatly accorded, harvests year after year ascended, and fathers and sons throughout the realm were at last able to support one another.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, through Your Majesty's supreme virtue in soothing and settling the people, the frontiers were secured, the heartland was at peace, yin and yang were in great harmony, harvests succeeded one another, and fathers and sons throughout the realm were at last able to support one another.

sentences.zh: 揚州構禍，殆有五旬，而海中晏然，纖塵不動，豈非天下蒸庶厭凶亂哉？

translations.literal: When Yangzhou raised calamity, it lasted nearly fifty days, yet within the seas all was calm—not a speck of dust stirred. Is this not because the common masses of the realm are weary of calamity and disorder?
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Yangzhou, it lasted nearly fifty days, yet the rest of the realm remained tranquil—not a ripple stirred. Is this not because the people are weary of calamity and disorder?

sentences.zh: 臣以此卜之，百姓思安久矣。

translations.literal: Your servant takes this as a divination: the common people have long yearned for peace.
translations.idiomatic: From this I infer that the people have long yearned for peace.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不務玄默，以救疲民，而又任威刑以失其望，欲以察察為政，肅理寰區。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not devote himself to profound stillness to rescue the weary people, yet again relies on stern punishments and thereby loses their hopes, wishing to govern through minute scrutiny and sternly order the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty does not cultivate quiet governance to relieve a weary people, but instead relies on harsh punishments and thereby forfeits their hopes, seeking to rule through relentless scrutiny and stern discipline across the realm.

sentences.zh: 愚臣暗昧，竊有大惑。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant is dim and obscure, and privately harbors great perplexity.
translations.idiomatic: I am but a dull and ignorant subject, and I confess to deep perplexity.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞刑者，政之末節也。

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant has heard that punishments are the final branch of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have heard that punishment is the last resort of government.

sentences.zh: 先王以禁暴厘亂，不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Former kings used them to restrain violence and set right disorder, employing them only when they had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old used punishments only to restrain violence and set right disorder, resorting to them only when they had no choice.

sentences.zh: 今天下幸安，萬物思泰，陛下乃以末節之法，察理平人，愚臣以為非適變隨時之義也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is fortunately at peace and all things yearn for tranquility, yet Your Majesty uses methods of the final branch to scrutinize and judge ordinary people. Your foolish servant considers this not the principle of adapting to change and following the times.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is fortunately at peace and all things yearn for tranquility, yet Your Majesty applies these last-resort methods to scrutinize ordinary people. I believe this fails the principle of adapting policy to the times.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，伏見諸方告密。

translations.literal: In recent years, your servant has humbly observed denunciations from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, I have observed denunciations pouring in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 囚累百千輩。

translations.literal: Prisoners accumulate by the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners have accumulated by the hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 大抵所告，皆以揚州為名，及其窮竟，百無一實。

translations.literal: For the most part, what was denounced all invoked Yangzhou by name, yet when fully investigated to the end, not one in a hundred proved true.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part, the accusations all invoked Yangzhou by name, yet when fully investigated, scarcely one in a hundred proved true.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁恕，又屈法容之，傍訐他事，亦為推劾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, being benevolent and forgiving, again bent the law to tolerate them, yet side matters were dug up and likewise subjected to investigation and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, being benevolent and forgiving, bent the law to spare them, yet other matters were dug up on the side and likewise subjected to investigation.

sentences.zh: 遂使奸臣之党，快意相讎，睚眥之嫌，即稱有密。

translations.literal: Thus the factions of treacherous ministers took satisfaction in mutual vengeance; a grudge no wider than an eyelash was at once declared a secret denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus factions of treacherous ministers took satisfaction in mutual vengeance; the slightest grudge was at once declared a secret denunciation.

sentences.zh: 一人被告，百人滿獄。

translations.literal: When one person was accused, a hundred filled the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: When one person was accused, a hundred filled the prisons.

sentences.zh: 使者推捕，冠蓋如市。

translations.literal: Envoys pursued and arrested; official carriages and canopies were like a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators pursued and arrested; official carriages thronged the roads like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 或謂陛下愛一人而害百人，天下喁喁，莫知寧所。

translations.literal: Some say Your Majesty loves one person yet harms a hundred; throughout the realm people murmur, not knowing where to find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Your Majesty spares one person yet harms a hundred; throughout the realm people murmur in alarm, not knowing where they may rest in peace.

sentences.zh: 臣聞自非聖人，不有外患，必有內憂，物理自然也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that unless one is a sage, if there is no external calamity, there must be internal worry—such is the natural principle of things.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that unless one is a sage, if there is no external threat, there will be internal trouble—such is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢以古遠言之，請指隋而說。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not speak from remote antiquity; please allow him to point to the Sui and speak.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not speak from remote antiquity; permit me to point to the Sui and speak.

sentences.zh: 臣聞長老云：隋之末世，天下猶平。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard elders say: in the final years of the Sui, the realm was still at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard elders say that in the final years of the Sui, the realm was still at peace.

sentences.zh: 煬帝不恭，窮毒威武，厭居皇極，自總元戎，以百萬之師，觀兵遼海，天下始騷然矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was irreverent, exhausting cruelty and martial might, weary of dwelling at the imperial apex; he personally commanded the main army and, with forces of a million, displayed arms at the Liao Sea—then the realm first grew turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was irreverent, exhausting cruelty and martial display; weary of the throne, he personally took command of the army and, with a million troops, paraded his forces at the Liao Sea—then the realm first grew turbulent.

sentences.zh: 遂使楊玄感挾不臣之勢，有大盜之心，欲因人謀，以竊皇業。

translations.literal: Thus Yang Xuangan seized the momentum of disloyalty, harbored the heart of a great bandit, and wished through others' plotting to steal the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yang Xuangan seized the momentum of rebellion, harbored the heart of a great bandit, and sought through others' plotting to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 及稱兵中夏，將據洛陽，哮寔之勢傾宇宙矣。

translations.literal: When he raised arms in central China and was about to seize Luoyang, the roaring force of his uprising shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: When he raised arms in central China and was about to seize Luoyang, the thunder of his rebellion seemed to shake heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 然亂未逾月，而頭足異處。

translations.literal: Yet the disorder had not passed a month before head and feet were in different places.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebellion had not lasted a month before his head and body lay in different places.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 天下之弊，未有土崩，蒸人之心，猶望樂業。

translations.literal: The realm's ills had not yet reached earth-collapse; the hearts of the common masses still hoped to enjoy their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's ills had not yet reached the point of collapse; the hearts of the people still hoped to live in peace.

sentences.zh: 煬帝不悟，暗忽人機。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang did not understand, but dimly neglected the workings of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang failed to understand; he blindly ignored the temper of the people.

sentences.zh: 自以為元惡既誅，天下無巨猾也，皇極之任，可以刑罰理之。

translations.literal: He thought that since the arch-criminal had already been executed, there were no great scoundrels left in the realm, and that the burden of the imperial apex could be managed through punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He thought that with the chief rebel already executed, no great scoundrels remained in the realm, and that the throne could be secured through punishments alone.

sentences.zh: 遂使兵部尚書樊子蓋專行屠戮，大窮黨與，海內豪士，無不罹殃。

translations.literal: He therefore had Minister of War Fan Zigai carry out slaughter exclusively, exhaustively pursuing factions and associates; eminent men throughout the realm none escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had Minister of War Fan Zigai carry out wholesale slaughter, exhaustively pursuing factions and associates until eminent men throughout the realm none escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 遂至殺人如麻，流血成澤，天下靡然思為亂矣。

translations.literal: It reached the point that men were killed like hemp stalks and blood formed marshes; throughout the realm all at once wished to rise in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: It reached the point that men were killed like hemp stalks and blood pooled like marshes; throughout the realm all at once wished to rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於是蕭銑、硃粲起于荊南，李密、竇建德亂于河北。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiao Xian and Zhu Can rose in southern Jing, while Li Mi and Dou Jiande stirred disorder in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xiao Xian and Zhu Can rose in southern Jing, while Li Mi and Dou Jiande stirred rebellion in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 四海雲搖，遂並起而亡隋族矣。

translations.literal: Within the four seas clouds shook; they then all rose together and extinguished the Sui house.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas turmoil spread; they then rose together and extinguished the house of Sui.

sentences.zh: 豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 長老至今談之，委曲如是。

translations.literal: Elders speak of it to this day; the full account is just so.
translations.idiomatic: Elders speak of it to this day; the full account is just as I have told it.

sentences.zh: 觀三代夏、殷興亡，已下至秦、漢、魏、晉理亂，莫不皆以毒刑而致敗壞也。

translations.literal: Observing the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties, Xia and Yin, down to the order and disorder of Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin—none failed to ruin themselves through poisonous punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties of Xia and Yin, down through the order and disorder of Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin—none failed to ruin themselves through cruel punishments.

sentences.zh: 夫大獄一起，不能無濫。

translations.literal: When great prosecutions arise, there cannot fail to be abuse.
translations.idiomatic: When great prosecutions arise, abuse cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 刀筆之吏，寡識大方，斷獄能者，名在急刻。

translations.literal: Clerks wielding brush and knife know little of the larger pattern; those skilled at deciding cases win renown for harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: Petty clerks know little of the larger pattern; those skilled at deciding cases win renown for harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 文深網密，則共稱至公，爰及人主，亦謂其奉法。

translations.literal: When legal language is deep and nets are dense, all together praise it as utmost fairness; reaching even the sovereign, he too considers it upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: When legal language is dense and the net of prosecution tight, all praise it as utmost fairness; even the sovereign considers it faithful adherence to law.

sentences.zh: 於是利在殺人，害在平恕，故獄吏相誡，以殺為詞。

translations.literal: Thus profit lay in killing people and harm lay in leniency and forgiveness; therefore prison officials admonished one another, taking killing as their theme.
translations.idiomatic: Thus profit lay in killing and harm lay in leniency; therefore prison officials admonished one another to make killing their watchword.

sentences.zh: 非憎於人也，而利在己。

translations.literal: It was not hatred of people, but profit for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: It was not hatred of people, but profit for themselves.

sentences.zh: 故上以希人主之旨，以圖榮身之利。

translations.literal: Therefore upward to match the sovereign's intent, and to plot personal advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Upward they sought to match the sovereign's intent; for themselves they plotted personal advancement.

sentences.zh: 徇利既多，則不能無濫，濫及良善，則淫刑逞矣。

translations.literal: Once pursuit of profit became widespread, abuse could not be avoided; when abuse reached the good and upright, excessive punishments ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Once pursuit of profit became widespread, abuse could not be avoided; when abuse reached the innocent, excessive punishments ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不自愛其身，陛下以此察之，豈非無濫矣！

translations.literal: Human feeling is such that none fail to cherish their own persons; if Your Majesty scrutinizes by this standard, is this not free of abuse!
translations.idiomatic: Human nature is such that all cherish their own lives; if Your Majesty scrutinizes by this standard, can there truly be no abuse!

sentences.zh: 冤人籲嗟，感傷和氣；

translations.literal: Wronged people cry out in lament, injuring harmonious qi;
translations.idiomatic: When the wronged cry out in lament, harmonious qi is injured;

sentences.zh: 和氣悖亂，群生癘疫；

translations.literal: when harmonious qi is perverse and disordered, the myriad beings suffer pestilence;
translations.idiomatic: when harmonious qi is disturbed, pestilence afflicts the people;

sentences.zh: 水旱隨之，則有凶年。

translations.literal: flood and drought follow, and then there are famine years.
translations.idiomatic: flood and drought follow, and famine years ensue.

sentences.zh: 人既失業，則禍亂之心怵然而生矣。

translations.literal: Once people lose their livelihoods, hearts of calamity and disorder suddenly arise.
translations.idiomatic: Once people lose their livelihoods, hearts of rebellion suddenly stir.

sentences.zh: 頃來亢陽愆候，雲而不雨，農夫釋耒，瞻望嗷嗷，豈不由陛下之有聖德而不降澤於人也？

translations.literal: Recently scorching yang has violated the seasons: clouds gather yet no rain falls; farmers lay down their plows and look up in desperate longing—is this not because Your Majesty possesses sage virtue yet fails to send down nourishing rain upon the people?
translations.idiomatic: Recently drought has violated the seasons: clouds gather yet no rain falls; farmers lay down their plows and look up in desperate longing—is this not because Your Majesty possesses sage virtue yet fails to send down nourishing rain upon the people?

sentences.zh: 儻旱遂過春，廢于時種，今年稼穡，必有損矣。

translations.literal: If the drought should pass into spring and planting for the season be abandoned, this year's harvest will surely suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: If drought should persist past spring and planting be abandoned, this year's harvest will surely suffer.

sentences.zh: 陛下可不敬承天意，以澤恤人？

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty fail reverently to receive Heaven's intent and thereby nourish and comfort the people?
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty not reverently heed Heaven's intent and thereby nourish and comfort the people?

sentences.zh: 臣聞古者明王重慎刑罰，蓋懼此也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in antiquity enlightened kings heavily weighed punishments—surely they feared this.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that enlightened kings of antiquity treated punishments with great caution—surely they feared this.

sentences.zh: 《書》不雲乎，「與其殺不辜，寧失不經。

translations.literal: Does not the Documents say: "Better to err in not executing than to kill the innocent"—
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Documents say: "Better to err in excess of leniency than to put the innocent to death"—

sentences.zh: 」陛下奈何以堂堂之聖，猶務強國之威。

translations.literal: "—yet how can Your Majesty, with such august sagehood, still pursue the majesty of a strong state?
translations.idiomatic: "—yet how can Your Majesty, with such august sagehood, still pursue the majesty of a strong state?

sentences.zh: 愚臣竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant privately considers this unworthy of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I privately consider this unworthy of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且愚人安則樂生，危則思變。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the foolish masses are secure they delight in life; when imperiled they think of change.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the common people are secure they delight in life; when imperiled they think of change.

sentences.zh: 故事有招禍，法有起奸。

translations.literal: Thus affairs may summon calamity, and laws may breed treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Thus affairs may summon calamity, and laws may breed treachery.

sentences.zh: 倘大獄未休，支黨日廣，天下疑惑，相恐無辜，人情之變，不可不察。

translations.literal: If great prosecutions do not cease and factions daily widen, the realm will be filled with doubt and mutual fear of innocence; changes in human feeling cannot go unobserved.
translations.idiomatic: If great prosecutions do not cease and factions daily widen, the realm will fill with doubt and mutual fear for the innocent; changes in the temper of the people cannot go unobserved.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝時巫蠱獄起，江充行詐，作亂京師，至使太子奔走，兵交宮闕，無辜被害者以萬千數。

translations.literal: Formerly in the time of Emperor Wu of Han the witchcraft prosecution arose; Jiang Chong practiced deceit and stirred disorder in the capital, until the crown prince fled and arms clashed at the palace gates; innocents harmed numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the time of Emperor Wu of Han the witchcraft prosecution arose; Jiang Chong practiced deceit and stirred disorder in the capital, until the crown prince fled and arms clashed at the palace gates; innocents harmed numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 當時劉宗幾覆滅矣，賴武帝得壺關三老上書，幡然感悟，夷江充三族，餘獄不論，天下少以安耳。

translations.literal: At that time the house of Liu was nearly extinguished; fortunately Emperor Wu received the memorial of the Three Elders of Huguan, suddenly awakened in understanding, exterminated Jiang Chong's three clans, and did not pursue the remaining cases—only then did the realm find some peace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the house of Liu was nearly extinguished; fortunately Emperor Wu received the memorial of the Three Elders of Huguan, suddenly awakened in understanding, exterminated Jiang Chong's three clans, and did not pursue the remaining cases—only then did the realm find some peace.

sentences.zh: 臣讀書至此，未嘗不為戾太子流涕也。

translations.literal: When your servant reads to this point in books, he has never failed to shed tears for Crown Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: When I read to this point in the histories, I have never failed to shed tears for Crown Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「前事不忘，後事之師。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Do not forget past affairs; they are teachers for later affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Do not forget past affairs; they are teachers for later affairs."

sentences.zh: 」伏願陛下念之。

translations.literal: " Your servant humbly hopes Your Majesty will keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: " I humbly hope Your Majesty will bear it in mind.

sentences.zh: 今臣不避湯鑊之罪，以螻蟻之命，輕觸宸嚴。

translations.literal: Now your servant does not avoid the crime of the boiling cauldron, but with the life of an ant lightly touches Your Majesty's august presence.
translations.idiomatic: Now I do not shrink from the boiling cauldron, but with my insignificant life lightly venture before Your Majesty's august presence.

sentences.zh: 臣非不惡死而貪生也，誠以負陛下恩遇，以微命蔽塞聰明，亦非敢欲陛下頓息嚴刑，望在恤刑耳。

translations.literal: Your servant is not one who does not hate death yet covets life; truly it is because he bears Your Majesty's gracious treatment and, with his slight life, would block Your Majesty's clear perception—nor does he dare wish Your Majesty suddenly to cease stern punishments; his hope lies only in compassionate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I do not hate death yet covet life; truly I bear Your Majesty's gracious treatment and would not with my slight life block Your Majesty's clear judgment—nor do I dare ask Your Majesty suddenly to cease stern punishments; my hope lies only in compassionate punishment.

sentences.zh: 乞與三事大夫，圖其可否。

translations.literal: I beg to join with the Three Affairs Grandees in deliberating its feasibility.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this be deliberated with the Three Affairs Grandees on its feasibility.

sentences.zh: 夫往者不可諫，來者猶可追，無以臣微而忽其奏，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: What is past cannot be remonstrated against; what is to come may still be pursued. Do not because your servant is insignificant neglect his memorial—the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: What is past cannot be remonstrated against; what is to come may still be pursued. Do not because I am insignificant neglect this memorial—the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 時司刑少卿徐有功常駁酷吏所奏，每日與之廷爭得失，以雪冤濫，因此全濟者亦不可勝數，語在《有功傳》。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Xu Yougong often rebutted what the harsh officials submitted, daily disputing with them in court over right and wrong to clear wrongful abuse; those thereby fully saved were also beyond counting—the account is in the Biography of Yougong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Xu Yougong often rebutted what the harsh officials submitted, daily disputing with them in court over right and wrong to clear wrongful prosecutions; those thereby fully saved were beyond counting—the account is in the Biography of Yougong.

sentences.zh: 及俊臣、弘義等伏誅，刑獄稍息。

translations.literal: When Jun Chen, Hongyi, and others were executed, penal prosecutions gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun Chen, Hongyi, and others were executed, penal prosecutions gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 前後宰相王及善、姚元崇、硃敬則等，皆言垂拱已來身死破家者，皆是枉濫，則天頗亦覺悟。

translations.literal: Successive chancellors Wang Jishan, Yao Yuanchong, Zhu Jingze, and others all said that since the Chui Gong era those who died or lost their families had all been wrongfully abused; Empress Wu then also somewhat awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Successive chancellors Wang Jishan, Yao Yuanchong, Zhu Jingze, and others all said that since the Chui Gong era those who died or lost their families had all been wrongfully prosecuted; Empress Wu then also somewhat awakened.

sentences.zh: 於是監察御史魏靖上言曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Investigating Censor Wei Jing submitted a statement, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Investigating Censor Wei Jing submitted a statement, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國之綱紀，在乎生殺。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that a state's fundamental order lies in life and death.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state's fundamental order lies in the power of life and death.

sentences.zh: 其周興、來俊臣、丘神勣、萬國俊、王弘義、侯思止、郭弘霸、李敬仁、彭先覺、王德壽、張知默者，即堯年四凶矣。

translations.literal: Such men as Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wan Guojun, Wang Hongyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Peng Xianjue, Wang Deshou, and Zhang Zhimò were the Four Evils of Yao's age.
translations.idiomatic: Such men as Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wan Guojun, Wang Hongyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Peng Xianjue, Wang Deshou, and Zhang Zhimò were the Four Evils of Yao's age.

sentences.zh: 恣騁愚暴，縱虐含毒，讎嫉在位，安忍朝臣，罪逐情加，刑隨意改。

translations.literal: They unrestrainedly galloped in folly and cruelty, indulged in torment and harbored poison, envied and hated those in office, and cruelly endured court ministers; crimes followed sentiment in increase, punishments followed whim in alteration.
translations.idiomatic: They unrestrainedly indulged folly and cruelty, tormented others and harbored malice, envied and hated those in office, and cruelly abused court ministers; crimes were inflated at whim and punishments altered at will.

sentences.zh: 當其時也，囚囹如市，朝廷以目。

translations.literal: In their time, prisons were like marketplaces and the court communicated by eye.
translations.idiomatic: In their time, prisons were like marketplaces and the court communicated only by glances.

sentences.zh: 既而素虛不昧，冤魂有托，行惡其報，禍淫可懲，具嚴天刑，以懲亂首。

translations.literal: Then plain truth was not obscured, wronged souls found refuge, evil deeds met their recompense, and the wicked could be punished; full severity of Heaven's punishment was applied to chastise the leaders of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Then plain truth was not obscured, wronged souls found refuge, evil deeds met their recompense, and the wicked were punished; Heaven's full severity was applied to chastise the leaders of disorder.

sentences.zh: 竊見來俊臣身處極法者，以其羅織良善，屠陷忠賢，籍沒以勸將來，顯戮以謝天下。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed that Lai Junchen suffered the utmost penalty because he fabricated charges against the good, slaughtered and entrapped the loyal and worthy, confiscated property to warn the future, and displayed execution to apologize to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Lai Junchen suffered the utmost penalty because he fabricated charges against the innocent, slaughtered and entrapped the loyal and worthy, confiscated property to warn the future, and was publicly executed to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之道路，上至聖主，傍洎貴臣，明明知有羅織之事矣，俊臣既死，推者獲功，胡元禮超遷，裴談顯授，中外稱慶，朝廷載安。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard on the roads that from the sage sovereign down to eminent ministers, all clearly knew there were fabricated prosecutions; once Junchen was dead, those who pursued cases gained merit—Hu Yuanli was promoted beyond measure, Pei Tan was conspicuously appointed—and within and without all praised the rejoicing; the court was again at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard on the roads that from the sage sovereign down to eminent ministers, all clearly knew there were fabricated prosecutions; once Junchen was dead, those who pursued cases gained merit—Hu Yuanli was promoted beyond measure, Pei Tan was conspicuously appointed—and within and without all rejoiced; the court was again at peace.

sentences.zh: 破其黨者，即能賞不逾時；

translations.literal: Those who broke their faction could at once be rewarded without delay;
translations.idiomatic: Those who broke their faction were rewarded without delay;

sentences.zh: 被其陷者，豈可淹之累歲。

translations.literal: those entrapped by them—how could they be detained for accumulated years?
translations.idiomatic: yet those entrapped by them—how could they be detained for years on end?

sentences.zh: 且稱反徒，須得反狀。

translations.literal: Moreover, to call someone a rebel requires obtaining evidence of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to call someone a rebel requires evidence of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 惟據片辭，即請行刑，拷楚妄加，款答何限。

translations.literal: Relying only on a fragment of words, they at once requested execution; torture was recklessly applied, and confessions—how limitless!
translations.idiomatic: Relying only on a fragment of testimony, they at once requested execution; torture was recklessly applied, and confessions—how limitless!

sentences.zh: 故徐有功以寬平而見忌，斛瑟羅以妓女而受拘，中外具知，枉直斯在，藉以為喻，其餘可詳。

translations.literal: Thus Xu Yougong was resented for leniency and fairness, and Khusro was detained on account of a courtesan; within and without all know where wrong and right lie—take these as examples; the rest may be told in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xu Yougong was resented for leniency and fairness, and Khusro was detained on account of a courtesan; within and without all know where wrong and right lie—take these as examples; the rest may be told in detail.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，郭弘霸自刺而唱快，萬國俊被遮而遽亡。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that Guo Hongba stabbed himself and cried out in satisfaction, and Wan Guojun, when intercepted, suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Guo Hongba stabbed himself and cried out in satisfaction, and Wan Guojun, when intercepted, suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 霍獻可臨終，膝拳于項；

translations.literal: Huo Xianké, at life's end, had knees drawn up to the neck;
translations.idiomatic: Huo Xianké, at life's end, had knees drawn up to his neck;

sentences.zh: 李敬仁將死，舌至於臍。

translations.literal: Li Jingren, about to die, had his tongue reach to his navel.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingren, about to die, had his tongue reach to his navel.

sentences.zh: 皆眾鬼滿庭，群妖橫道，惟徵集應，若響隨聲。

translations.literal: All were cases of ghosts filling the courtyard and demons blocking the road; omens gathered in response like echoes following sound.
translations.idiomatic: All were cases of ghosts filling the courtyard and demons blocking the road; omens gathered in response like echoes following sound.

sentences.zh: 備在人謠，不為虛說，伯有晝見，殆無以過。

translations.literal: Fully preserved in people's songs and tales, this is no empty talk; even Bo You appearing by day scarcely surpasses it.
translations.idiomatic: Fully preserved in people's songs and tales, this is no empty talk; even Bo You appearing by day scarcely surpasses it.

sentences.zh: 此亦羅織之一據也。

translations.literal: This too is one proof of fabricated prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: This too is proof of fabricated prosecution.

sentences.zh: 臣以至愚，不識大體，儻使平反者數人，眾共詳覆來俊臣等所推大獄，庶鄧艾獲申於今日，孝婦不濫于昔時，恩渙一流，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your servant, being utterly foolish and not knowing the larger pattern, humbly proposes that if several persons were appointed to reverse wrongful verdicts and all together thoroughly reviewed the great prosecutions pushed by Lai Junchen and others, perhaps Deng Ai might obtain vindication today and the dutiful wife would not be wrongfully condemned as in former times; grace would spread in one flow—the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I am utterly foolish and do not grasp the larger pattern, but if several persons were appointed to reverse wrongful verdicts and all together thoroughly reviewed the great prosecutions pushed by Lai Junchen and others, perhaps Deng Ai might be vindicated today and the dutiful wife would not be wrongfully condemned as in former times; grace would spread throughout the realm—the people would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，制令錄來俊臣、丘神勣等所推鞫人身死籍沒者，令三司重推勘，有冤濫者，並皆雪免。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered recording those prosecuted to death and confiscation of property by Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, and others, and commanded the Three Offices to reinvestigate; those wrongfully abused were all cleared and exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered a record of those prosecuted to death and stripped of property by Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, and others, and commanded the Three Offices to reinvestigate; those wrongfully prosecuted were all cleared and exonerated.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍元年，制以故司僕少卿徐有功，執法平恕，追贈越州都督，特授一子官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong under Emperor Zhongzong, an edict honored the late Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xu Yougong for fair and forgiving enforcement of law, posthumously enfeoffing him as Governor-General of Yuezhou and specially granting one son an office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong under Emperor Zhongzong, an edict honored the late Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xu Yougong for fair and forgiving enforcement of law, posthumously enfeoffing him as Governor-General of Yuezhou and specially granting one son an office.

sentences.zh: 又以丘神勣、來子珣、萬國俊、周興、來俊臣、魚承曄、王景昭、索元禮、傅遊藝、王弘義、張知默、裴籍、焦仁亶、侯思止、郭霸、李敬仁、皇甫文備、陳嘉言、劉光業、王德壽、王處貞、屈貞筠、鮑思恭二十三人，自垂拱已來並枉濫殺人，所有官爵，並令追奪。

translations.literal: It also ordered that the twenty-three men Qiu Shenji, Lai Zixun, Wan Guojun, Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Yu Chengye, Wang Jingzhao, Suo Yuanli, Fu Youyi, Wang Hongyi, Zhang Zhimò, Pei Ji, Jiao Renxuan, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Li Jingren, Huangfu Wenbei, Chen Jiayan, Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and Bao Sigong, who since the Chui Gong era had all wrongfully and abusively killed people, should have all their offices and enfeoffments retroactively stripped.
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered that the twenty-three men Qiu Shenji, Lai Zixun, Wan Guojun, Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Yu Chengye, Wang Jingzhao, Suo Yuanli, Fu Youyi, Wang Hongyi, Zhang Zhimò, Pei Ji, Jiao Renxuan, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Li Jingren, Huangfu Wenbei, Chen Jiayan, Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and Bao Sigong, who since the Chui Gong era had all wrongfully killed people, should have all their offices and enfeoffments retroactively stripped.

sentences.zh: 天下稱慶。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm people praised the rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 時既改易，制盡依貞觀、永徽故事。

translations.literal: Since the times had changed, edicts all followed the precedents of Zhenguan and Yonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Since the times had changed, edicts all followed the precedents of Zhenguan and Yonghui.

sentences.zh: 敕中書令韋安石、禮部侍郎祝欽明、尚書右丞蘇瑰、兵部郎中狄光嗣等，刪定《垂拱格》後至神龍元年已來制敕，為《散頒格》七卷。

translations.literal: An edict commanded Grand Counselor Wei Anshi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Zhu Qinming, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Su Gui, Bureau Director of the Ministry of War Di Guangsi, and others to revise and fix edicts from after the Chui Gong Regulations through the first year of Shenlong, forming seven fascicles of Broadly Promulgated Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded Grand Counselor Wei Anshi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Zhu Qinming, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Su Gui, Bureau Director of the Ministry of War Di Guangsi, and others to revise edicts from after the Chui Gong Regulations through the first year of Shenlong, forming seven fascicles of Broadly Promulgated Regulations.

sentences.zh: 又刪補舊式，為二十卷，頒於天下。

translations.literal: They also revised and supplemented the old forms into twenty fascicles and promulgated them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They also revised and supplemented the old forms into twenty fascicles and promulgated them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，睿宗又敕戶部尚書岑羲、中書侍郎陸象先、右散騎常侍徐堅、右司郎中唐紹、刑部員外郎邵知與、刪定官大理寺丞陳義海、右衛長史張處斌、大理評事張名播、左衛率府倉曹參軍羅思貞、刑部主事閻義顓凡十人，刪定格、式、律、令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun, Emperor Ruizong again commanded Minister of Revenue Cen Xi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Xiangxian, Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Xu Jian, Right Bureau Director Tang Shao, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Shao Zhiyu, revising official Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Yihai, Chief Secretary of the Right Guard Zhang Chubin, Judicial Review Evaluator Zhang Mingbo, Left Guard Rate-Fu Warehouse Section Officer Luo Sizhen, and Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Justice Yan Yizhuan—ten persons in all—to revise regulations, forms, statutes, and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingyun, Emperor Ruizong again commanded Minister of Revenue Cen Xi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Xiangxian, Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Xu Jian, Right Bureau Director Tang Shao, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Shao Zhiyu, revising official Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Yihai, Chief Secretary of the Right Guard Zhang Chubin, Judicial Review Evaluator Zhang Mingbo, Left Guard Rate-Fu Warehouse Section Officer Luo Sizhen, and Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Justice Yan Yizhuan—ten persons in all—to revise regulations, forms, statutes, and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 太極元年二月奏上，名為《太極格》。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taiji it was submitted and named the Taiji Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Taiji it was submitted and named the Taiji Regulations.

sentences.zh: 開元初，玄宗敕黃門監盧懷慎、紫微侍郎兼刑部尚書李乂、紫微侍郎蘇頲、紫微舍人呂延祚、給事中魏奉古、大理評事高智靜、同州韓城縣丞侯郢璡、瀛州司法參軍閻義顓等，刪定格、式、令，至三年三月奏上，名為《開元格》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong commanded Supervisor of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaiqian, Vice Director of the Purple Pavilion and concurrent Minister of Justice Li Yi, Vice Director of the Purple Pavilion Su Ting, Purple Pavilion Drafter Lü Yanzuo, Attendant within the Yellow Gate Wei Fenggu, Judicial Review Evaluator Gao Zhijing, Assistant Magistrate of Hancheng County in Tong Prefecture Hou Yingjin, and Legal Section Officer of Ying Prefecture Yan Yizhuan and others to revise regulations, forms, and ordinances; in the third month of the third year it was submitted and named the Kaiyuan Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong commanded Supervisor of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaiqian, Vice Director of the Purple Pavilion and concurrent Minister of Justice Li Yi, Vice Director of the Purple Pavilion Su Ting, Purple Pavilion Drafter Lü Yanzuo, Attendant within the Yellow Gate Wei Fenggu, Judicial Review Evaluator Gao Zhijing, Assistant Magistrate of Hancheng County in Tong Prefecture Hou Yingjin, and Legal Section Officer of Ying Prefecture Yan Yizhuan and others to revise regulations, forms, and ordinances; in the third month of the third year it was submitted and named the Kaiyuan Regulations.

sentences.zh: 六年，玄宗又敕吏部侍郎兼侍中宋璟、中書侍郎蘇頲、尚書左丞盧從願、吏部侍郎裴漼慕容珣、戶部侍郎楊滔、中書舍人劉令植、大理司直高智靜、幽州司功參軍侯郢璡等九人，刪定律、令、格、式，至七年三月奏上。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Emperor Xuanzong again commanded Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrent Palace Attendant Song Jing, Vice Director of the Secretariat Su Ting, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Congyuan, Vice Directors of the Ministry of Personnel Pei Cui and Murong Xun, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yang Tao, Secretariat Drafter Liu Lingzhi, Judicial Review Direct Examiner Gao Zhijing, and Merit Section Officer of You Prefecture Hou Yingjin—nine persons—to revise statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms; in the third month of the seventh year it was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Emperor Xuanzong again commanded Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrent Palace Attendant Song Jing, Vice Director of the Secretariat Su Ting, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Congyuan, Vice Directors of the Ministry of Personnel Pei Cui and Murong Xun, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yang Tao, Secretariat Drafter Liu Lingzhi, Judicial Review Direct Examiner Gao Zhijing, and Merit Section Officer of You Prefecture Hou Yingjin—nine persons—to revise statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms; in the third month of the seventh year it was submitted.

sentences.zh: 律、令、式仍舊名，格曰《開元後格》。

translations.literal: Statutes, ordinances, and forms kept their old names; the regulations were called the Post-Kaiyuan Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes, ordinances, and forms kept their old names; the regulations were called the Post-Kaiyuan Regulations.

sentences.zh: 十九年，侍中裴光庭、中書令蕭嵩，又以格後制敕行用之後，頗與格文相違，於事非便，奏令所司刪撰《格後長行敕》六卷，頒於天下。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Chief Councilor Pei Guangting and Grand Counselor Xiao Song, again noting that after post-regulation edicts were put into practice they often conflicted considerably with the regulatory text and were inconvenient in affairs, memorialized ordering the responsible offices to compile and edit six fascicles of Long-standing Edicts after the Regulations and promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Chief Councilor Pei Guangting and Grand Counselor Xiao Song observed that once post-regulation edicts had been put into effect, they often clashed with the regulatory text and proved impractical in administration. They memorialized the throne to have the responsible offices compile six fascicles of Long-standing Edicts after the Regulations and distribute them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，戶部尚書李林甫又受詔改修格令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Minister of Revenue Li Linfu again received an edict to revise and edit the regulations and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Minister of Revenue Li Linfu received another imperial edict to revise the regulations and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 林甫遷中書令，乃與侍中牛仙客、御史中丞王敬從，與明法之官前左武衛胄曹參軍崔見、衛州司戶參軍直中書陳承信、酸棗尉直刑部俞元杞等，共加刪緝舊格、式、律、令及敕，總七千二十六條。

translations.literal: When Linfu was transferred to Grand Counselor, he then together with Chief Councilor Niu Xianke, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Jingcong, and legal specialists including former Left Martial Guard Army Section Officer Cui Jian, Wei Prefecture Registrar on special assignment to the Secretariat Chen Chengxin, Suozao District Magistrate on special assignment to the Ministry of Justice Yu Yuanqi, and others jointly added revision and compilation to the old regulations, forms, statutes, ordinances, and edicts—a total of seven thousand twenty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: After Linfu was promoted to Grand Counselor, he joined Chief Councilor Niu Xianke, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Jingcong, and legal specialists including former Left Martial Guard Army Section Officer Cui Jian, Wei Prefecture Registrar Chen Chengxin on special assignment to the Secretariat, Suozao District Magistrate Yu Yuanqi on special assignment to the Ministry of Justice, and others in revising the old regulations, forms, statutes, ordinances, and edicts—a total of 7,026 articles.

sentences.zh: 其一千三百二十四條於事非要，並刪之。

translations.literal: Of these, one thousand three hundred twenty-four articles were unnecessary for practical affairs and were all deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, 1,324 articles were deemed unnecessary in practice and were all removed.

sentences.zh: 二千一百八十條隨文損益，三千五百九十四條仍舊不改。

translations.literal: Two thousand one hundred eighty articles were amended according to the text; three thousand five hundred ninety-four articles remained as before without change.
translations.idiomatic: 2,180 articles were revised as the text required; 3,594 were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 總成律十二卷，《律疏》三十卷，《令》三十卷，《式》二十卷，《開元新格》十卷。

translations.literal: In total they formed twelve fascicles of statutes, thirty fascicles of Statutory Commentary, thirty fascicles of ordinances, twenty fascicles of forms, and ten fascicles of New Kaiyuan Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The work yielded twelve fascicles of statutes, thirty of Statutory Commentary, thirty of ordinances, twenty of forms, and ten of New Kaiyuan Regulations.

sentences.zh: 又撰《格式律令事類》四十卷，以類相從，便於省覽。

translations.literal: They also compiled forty fascicles of Categories of Regulations, Forms, Statutes, and Ordinances, arranged by category for convenient review.
translations.idiomatic: They also compiled forty fascicles of Categories of Regulations, Forms, Statutes, and Ordinances, grouping related matters together for easier consultation.

sentences.zh: 二十五年九月奏上，敕于尚書都省寫五十本，發使散於天下。
