translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year it was submitted; an edict ordered fifty copies written at the Executive Office of the Department of State Affairs and envoys dispatched to distribute them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It was submitted in the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year. An edict ordered fifty copies made at the Executive Office of the Department of State Affairs and dispatched envoys to distribute them across the realm.

sentences.zh: 其年刑部斷獄，天下死罪惟有五十八人。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Justice adjudicated cases; throughout the realm there were only fifty-eight persons sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Ministry of Justice adjudicated cases, only fifty-eight people throughout the realm were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿徐嶠上言：大理獄院，由來相傳殺氣太盛，鳥雀不棲，至是有鵲巢其樹。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Qiao submitted: "In the prison compound of the Court of Judicial Review, it has been handed down from old times that the killing atmosphere was too strong and birds would not perch; now magpies have nested in its trees."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Qiao reported: "In the prison yard of the Court of Judicial Review, tradition held that the air of death was so heavy birds would not alight there—yet now magpies have built nests in its trees."

sentences.zh: 於是百僚以幾至刑措，上表陳賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred officials, considering that punishments were nearly set aside, submitted memorials offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The officials then submitted memorials of congratulation, taking this as a sign that punishments were nearly unused.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以宰相變理、法官平允之功，封仙客為邠國公，林甫為晉國公，刑部大理官共賜帛二千匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, for the achievements of the chief ministers in transforming governance and the judicial officials in fairness and evenhandedness, enfeoffed Xianke as Duke of Bin and Linfu as Duke of Jin, and jointly granted officials of the Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong rewarded the chief ministers for transforming governance and the judicial officials for fair and evenhanded judgment by enfeoffing Xianke as Duke of Bin and Linfu as Duke of Jin, and granting officials of the Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review two thousand bolts of silk together.

sentences.zh: 自明慶至先天六十年間，高宗寬仁，政歸宮閫。

translations.literal: From the Mingqing era to the Xiantian era—a span of sixty years—Emperor Gaozong was lenient and humane, and government passed into the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Over the sixty years from the Mingqing era to the Xiantian era, Emperor Gaozong was lenient and humane, and power passed into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 則天女主猜忌，果于殺戮，宗枝大臣，鍛于酷吏，至於移易宗社，幾亡李氏。

translations.literal: Empress Wu as female sovereign was suspicious and jealous, ruthless in killing; imperial clansmen and great ministers were forged by cruel officials; the state foundation was even changed, and the House of Li nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, ruling as female sovereign, was suspicious and ruthless in bloodshed; imperial clansmen and great ministers were framed by cruel officials; the dynasty itself was nearly overturned, and the House of Li almost destroyed.

sentences.zh: 神龍之後，後族幹政，景雲繼立，歸妹怙權。

translations.literal: After Shenlong, the empress's clan interfered in government; Jingyun continued in succession; Guimei relied on power.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenlong restoration, the empress's clan meddled in government; under Jingyun the pattern continued, and Princess Guimei leaned on her power.

sentences.zh: 開元之際，刑政賞罰，斷於宸極，四十餘年，可謂太平矣。

translations.literal: At the Kaiyuan juncture, penal policy and rewards and punishments were decided at the imperial throne; for more than forty years it may be called peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, criminal policy and the dispensing of rewards and punishments were decided at the throne itself; for more than forty years the age could be called peaceful.

sentences.zh: 及塚臣懷邪，邊將內侮，乘輿幸于巴、蜀，儲副立于朔方，曾未逾年，載收京邑，書契以來，未有克復宗社若斯之速也。

translations.literal: When corrupt favorites harbored wickedness and frontier generals turned inward in contempt, the imperial carriage traveled to Ba and Shu and the heir apparent was established at Shuofang; before a year had passed the capital was retaken—in the history of writing since antiquity there had never been recovery of the ancestral temple so swift as this.
translations.idiomatic: When corrupt favorites at court turned wicked and frontier generals rose in rebellion, the emperor fled to Ba and Shu while the heir apparent was installed at Shuofang. In less than a year the capital was retaken—since the age of writing began, never had the dynasty been restored so swiftly.

sentences.zh: 而兩京衣冠，多被脅從，至是相率待罪闕下。

translations.literal: Yet the gentry of the two capitals had largely been coerced into following; now they came in succession to await judgment at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many officials of the two capitals had been coerced into following the rebels, and now they came in succession to the palace gates to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 而執事者務欲峻刑以取威，盡誅其族，以令天下。

translations.literal: But those in charge wished to use harsh punishments to gain authority, exterminate entire clans, and command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge, however, sought to impress the realm with harsh punishments, exterminate entire clans, and enforce obedience throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 議久不定，竟置三司使，以御史大夫兼京兆尹李峴、兵部侍郎呂諲、戶部侍郎兼御史中丞崔器、刑部侍郎兼御史中丞韓擇木、大理卿嚴向等五人為之。

translations.literal: Deliberation went on long without resolution; finally Three Offices commissioners were established, with the five men Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Governor of Jingzhao Li Xian, Vice Director of the Ministry of War Lü Yun, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief Han Zemu, and Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yan Xiang appointed to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Debate dragged on without resolution until Three Offices commissioners were finally appointed: Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Governor of Jingzhao Li Xian, Vice Director of the Ministry of War Lü Yun, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief Han Zemu, and Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yan Xiang—five men in all.

sentences.zh: 初，西京文武官陸大鈞等陷賊來歸，崔器草儀，盡令免冠徒跣，撫膺號泣，以金吾府縣人吏圍之，於朝謝罪，收付大理京兆府獄系之。

translations.literal: Initially, when civil and military officials of the Western Capital such as Lu Dajun who had fallen into the rebels' hands returned, Cui Qi drafted the ceremony and ordered all to remove caps and go barefoot, beating their breasts and wailing; Golden Guard and county clerks encircled them; at court they thanked for their crimes and were taken into custody in the prisons of the Court of Judicial Review and Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when civil and military officials of the Western Capital such as Lu Dajun who had fallen into rebel hands returned, Cui Qi drafted the ceremony and ordered them all to remove their caps and go barefoot, beating their breasts and wailing. Golden Guard and county clerks encircled them; at court they confessed their guilt and were handed over to the prisons of the Court of Judicial Review and Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及陳希烈等大臣至者數百人，又令朝堂徒跣如初，令宰相苗晉卿、崔圓、李麟等百僚同視，以為棄辱，宣詔以責之。

translations.literal: When several hundred great ministers including Chen Xilie arrived, they were again ordered to go barefoot in court as before; the chief ministers Miao Jinqing, Cui Yuan, Li Lin, and the hundred officials were made to look on together; deeming this abandonment and humiliation, an edict was promulgated to rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: When several hundred great ministers including Chen Xilie arrived, they were again made to go barefoot in court as before, while Chief Ministers Miao Jinqing, Cui Yuan, Li Lin, and the rest of the officials were forced to watch. Considering this an outrage and humiliation, an edict was issued rebuking them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又以負罪者眾，獄中不容，乃賜楊國忠宅鞫之。

translations.literal: The court also considered that those guilty were numerous and the prisons could not hold them, so Yang Guozhong's residence was granted for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Because so many were under accusation and the prisons could not hold them all, the court granted Yang Guozhong's residence for interrogations.

sentences.zh: 器、諲多希旨深刻，而擇木無所是非，獨李峴力爭之，乃定所推之罪為六等，集百僚尚書省議之。

translations.literal: Qi and Yun largely sought to please the throne and were severe; Zemu had no positions on right and wrong; only Li Xian argued forcefully; they then fixed the recommended crimes in six grades and assembled the hundred officials at the Department of State Affairs to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi and Lü Yun largely sought to please the throne and pursued harsh sentences; Han Zemu took no clear stand; only Li Xian argued forcefully. They then fixed the recommended crimes in six grades and assembled the officials at the Department of State Affairs to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 肅宗方用刑名，公卿但唯唯署名而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was then employing penal law; the high ministers simply assented and signed their names.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was then ruling through harsh penal law, and the high ministers simply assented and signed their names.

sentences.zh: 於是河南尹達奚珣等三十九人，以為罪重，與從共棄。

translations.literal: Thereupon thirty-nine persons including Governor of Henan Dati Xun, considering the crimes heavy, were together condemned and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-nine men, including Governor of Henan Dati Xun, were judged guilty of grave crimes and condemned together with their followers.

sentences.zh: 珣等十一人，於子城西伏誅。

translations.literal: Eleven persons including Xun were executed in secret west of Zi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven of them, including Xun, were secretly executed west of Zi Gate.

sentences.zh: 陳希烈、張垍、郭納、獨孤朗等七人，於大理寺獄賜自盡。

translations.literal: Seven persons including Chen Xilie, Zhang Ya, Guo Na, and Dugu Lang were granted suicide in the prison of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Seven men—Chen Xilie, Zhang Ya, Guo Na, Dugu Lang, and others—were granted permission to take their own lives in the prison of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 達奚摯、張岯、李有孚、劉子英、冉大華二十一人，於京兆府門決重杖死。

translations.literal: Twenty-one persons including Dati Zhi, Zhang Bi, Li Youfu, Liu Ziying, and Ran Dahua were beaten to death with heavy rods at the gate of Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one men—including Dati Zhi, Zhang Bi, Li Youfu, Liu Ziying, and Ran Dahua—were beaten to death with heavy rods at the gate of Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大理卿張均引至獨柳樹下刑人處，免死配流合浦郡，而達奚珣、韋恆乃至腰斬。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Jun led them to the execution ground beneath the lone willow tree; death was spared and they were sentenced to exile in Hepu Commandery—but Dati Xun and Wei Heng were even cut at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Jun led others to the execution ground beneath the lone willow tree, where they were spared death and sentenced to exile in Hepu Commandery—but Dati Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 先是，慶緒至相州，史思明、高秀岩等皆送款請命，肅宗各令復位，便領所管，至是懼不自安，各率其黨叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qingxu arrived at Xiangzhou, Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others all offered submission and pleaded for their lives; Emperor Suzong ordered each restored to office and to lead their jurisdictions; now, fearing and ill at ease, each led his faction in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qingxu reached Xiangzhou, Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others had all submitted and pleaded for their lives. Emperor Suzong restored each to office and left him in command of his territory. Now, fearing for their safety, each led his followers in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其後三司用刑，連年不定，流貶相繼。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Three Offices applied punishments year after year without resolution; exile and demotion followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Three Offices kept applying punishments year after year without bringing cases to resolution, and exile and demotion followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 及王璵為相，素聞物議，請下詔自今已後，三司推勘未畢者，一切放免，大收人望。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu became chief minister, having long heard public criticism, he requested an edict that from now on all those whose cases the Three Offices had not yet finished investigating should be wholly released and pardoned, greatly gaining popular esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yu became chief minister, having long heard public criticism, he requested an edict that from then on all cases still under investigation by the Three Offices should be wholly dismissed and pardoned—a move that greatly won popular esteem.

sentences.zh: 後蕭華拔魏州歸國，嘗話於朝云：「初河北官聞國家宣詔放陳希列等脅從官一切不問，各令復位，聞者悔歸國之晚，舉措自失。

translations.literal: Later when Xiao Hua took Weizhou and returned to allegiance, he once spoke at court saying: "Initially, when officials in Hebei heard the state's proclamation releasing all coerced followers of Chen Xilie and others without question and restoring each to office, those who heard it regretted returning to allegiance so late and lost their bearings in action."
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Xiao Hua recovered Weizhou and returned to allegiance, he once told the court: "At first, when officials in Hebei heard the state's proclamation that all coerced followers of Chen Xilie and others would be released without question and restored to office, those who heard it regretted having delayed their return and lost their bearings."

sentences.zh: 及後聞希烈等死，皆相賀得計，無敢歸者。

translations.literal: "After they later heard that Xilie and others had died, all congratulated one another on having judged rightly; none dared return."
translations.idiomatic: "But when they later heard that Xilie and others had been executed, they congratulated one another on having judged wisely—and none dared return."

sentences.zh: 於是河北將吏，人人益堅，大兵不解。

translations.literal: "Thereupon the generals and officials of Hebei, each man grew firmer; the great army could not be disbanded."
translations.idiomatic: "Thereupon the generals and officials of Hebei grew only more resolute, and the great armies could not be stood down."

sentences.zh: 後有毛若虛、敬羽之流，皆深酷割剝，驟求權柄，殺人以逞刑，厚斂以資國。

translations.literal: Later there were men like Mao Ruoxu and Jing Yu, all deeply cruel in extortion, suddenly seeking power; they killed people to wield punishment and heavily levied to supply the state.
translations.idiomatic: Later came men like Mao Ruoxu and Jing Yu—deeply cruel in extortion, suddenly grasping for power, killing to wield the law, and levying heavily to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 六七年間，大獄相繼，州縣之內，多是貶降人。

translations.literal: Over six or seven years great prosecutions followed in succession; within prefectures and counties most were demoted and exiled persons.
translations.idiomatic: Over six or seven years major prosecutions followed one after another, and in prefectures and counties most of those caught up in them were demoted or exiled.

sentences.zh: 肅宗復聞三司多濫，嘗悔云：「朕為三司所誤，深恨之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong again heard that the Three Offices were largely abusive; he once regretted, saying: "We were misled by the Three Offices and deeply resent it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong again heard how abusive the Three Offices had become and once lamented: "I was misled by the Three Offices, and I deeply regret it."

sentences.zh: 」及彌留之際，以元載為相，乃詔天下流降人等一切放歸。

translations.literal: "At the final illness, with Yuan Zai as chief minister, an edict ordered all exiled and demoted persons throughout the realm to be released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: At his final illness, with Yuan Zai as chief minister, he issued an edict ordering all exiled and demoted persons throughout the realm to be released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 代宗寶應元年，回紇與史朝義戰，勝，擒其將士妻子老幼四百八十人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying under Emperor Daizong, the Uyghurs fought Shi Chaoyi, won, and captured four hundred eighty persons including generals, soldiers, wives, children, old and young.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying under Emperor Daizong, the Uyghurs fought Shi Chaoyi and won, capturing 480 people—generals, soldiers, wives, children, old and young.

sentences.zh: 上以婦人雖為賊家口，皆是良家子女，被賊逼略，惻然湣之，令萬年縣於勝業佛寺安置，給糧料。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that although the women were rebel household members, all were daughters of good families forced and taken by bandits; he felt pity and ordered Wannian County to settle them at Shengye Buddhist Temple and provide grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered that although the women were counted as rebel household members, all were daughters of respectable families seized by force. Moved with pity, he ordered Wannian County to settle them at Shengye Buddhist Temple and provide grain rations.

sentences.zh: 若有親屬認者，任還之；

translations.literal: If relatives came to claim them, they were permitted to be returned;
translations.idiomatic: If relatives came forward to claim them, they were permitted to take them back;

sentences.zh: 如無親族者，任其所適，仍給糧遞過。

translations.literal: if there were no kin, they were permitted to go where they wished, and grain for traveling post stations was still provided.
translations.idiomatic: if they had no kin, they were free to go where they wished, and grain for traveling post stations was still provided.

sentences.zh: 於是人情莫不感戴忻悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon popular sentiment without exception was grateful and rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people were universally grateful and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年六月一日，德宗禦丹鳳樓大赦。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Dali, Emperor Dezong held a great amnesty at Danfeng Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month in the fourteenth year of Dali, Emperor Dezong proclaimed a great amnesty from Danfeng Tower.

sentences.zh: 赦書節文：「律、令、格、式條目有未折衷者，委中書門下簡擇理識通明官共刪定。

translations.literal: An excerpt from the amnesty document: "Where articles of statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms have not been harmonized, commission the Secretariat-Chancellery to select officials of penetrating reason and understanding to jointly revise and fix them."
translations.idiomatic: An excerpt from the amnesty document read: "Where articles of statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms remain unreconciled, commission the Secretariat-Chancellery to select clear-minded officials to revise and fix them together."

sentences.zh: 自至德已來制敕，或因人奏請，或臨事頒行，差互不同，使人疑惑，中書門下與刪定官詳決，取堪久長行用者，編入格條。

translations.literal: "Edicts since the Zhide era, whether arising from individual memorials or promulgated on the spot for particular affairs, differ inconsistently and cause people doubt; the Secretariat-Chancellery together with the revising officials shall examine and decide in detail, take those suitable for long-term use, and compile them into regulatory articles."
translations.idiomatic: "Edicts since the Zhide era, whether arising from individual petitions or issued on the spot for particular affairs, differ inconsistently and cause confusion. The Secretariat-Chancellery, together with the revising officials, shall examine them in detail, select those suitable for long-term use, and compile them into regulatory articles."

sentences.zh: 」三司使，准式以御史中丞、中書舍人、給事中各一人為之，每日於朝堂受詞，推勘處分。

translations.literal: "Three Offices commissioners, according to the form, shall consist of one Vice Censor-in-Chief, one Secretariat Drafter, and one Attendant within, each day receiving petitions at court and investigating and disposing of cases."
translations.idiomatic: "Three Offices commissioners, according to established procedure, shall consist of one Vice Censor-in-Chief, one Secretariat Drafter, and one Attendant within, who each day receive petitions at court and investigate and dispose of cases."

sentences.zh: 建中二年，罷刪定格令使並三司使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, the commissioners for revising regulations and ordinances and the Three Offices commissioners were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong, the commissioners for revising regulations and ordinances and the Three Offices commissioners were abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是，以中書門下充刪定格令使，又以給事中、中書舍人、御史中丞為三司使。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Secretariat-Chancellery had served as commissioners for revising regulations and ordinances, and Attendants within, Secretariat Drafters, and Vice Censor-in-Chief had served as Three Offices commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the Secretariat-Chancellery had served as commissioners for revising regulations and ordinances, while Attendants within, Secretariat Drafters, and Vice Censor-in-Chief had served as Three Offices commissioners.

sentences.zh: 至是中書門下奏請復舊，以刑部、御史臺、大理寺為之。

translations.literal: At this time the Secretariat-Chancellery memorialized requesting restoration of the old practice, with the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, and Court of Judicial Review serving as the offices.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the Secretariat-Chancellery memorialized to restore the old arrangement, with the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, and Court of Judicial Review taking up the role.

sentences.zh: 其格令委刑部刪定。

translations.literal: The regulations and ordinances were entrusted to the Ministry of Justice for revision and fixing.
translations.idiomatic: Revision of the regulations and ordinances was entrusted to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元和四年九月敕：「刑部大理決斷系囚，過為淹遲，是長奸幸。

translations.literal: An edict of the ninth month of the fourth year of Yuanhe: "The Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review in deciding and sentencing imprisoned persons are overly delayed—this fosters villainy and luck."
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the ninth month in the fourth year of Yuanhe declared: "The Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review take too long to decide cases of imprisoned persons—this only encourages wrongdoing and evasion."

sentences.zh: 自今已後，大理寺檢斷，不得過二十日，刑部覆下，不得過十日。

translations.literal: "From now on, examination and judgment by the Court of Judicial Review may not exceed twenty days; review and transmission by the Ministry of Justice may not exceed ten days."
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth, the Court of Judicial Review may take no more than twenty days to examine and decide a case, and the Ministry of Justice no more than ten days to review and transmit the decision."

sentences.zh: 如刑部覆有異同，寺司重加不得過十五日，省司量覆不得過本日。

translations.literal: "If the Ministry of Justice's review finds disagreement, re-examination by the court may not exceed fifteen days; review in the Department may not exceed that same day."
translations.idiomatic: "If the Ministry of Justice's review finds disagreement, the court may take no more than fifteen days for re-examination, and the Department no more than that same day for its review."

sentences.zh: 如有牒外州府節目及於京城內勘，本推即日以報。

translations.literal: "If there are matters requiring investigation outside the capital in prefectures or within the capital itself, the original investigating office shall report on the same day."
translations.idiomatic: "If a case requires investigation in an outside prefecture or within the capital itself, the original investigating office shall report on the same day."

sentences.zh: 牒到後計日數，被勘司卻報不得過五日。

translations.literal: "After the dispatch arrives, counting days, the investigated office's return report may not exceed five days."
translations.idiomatic: "Once the dispatch arrives, the investigated office's reply may take no more than five days."

sentences.zh: 仍令刑部具遣牒及報牒月日，牒報都省及分察使，各准敕文勾舉糾訪。

translations.literal: "Moreover order the Ministry of Justice to record the month and day of dispatch and return dispatches, and notify the Executive Office and branch inspectors; each shall verify and investigate according to the edict text."
translations.idiomatic: "The Ministry of Justice shall also record the dates of outgoing and returning dispatches and notify the Executive Office and branch inspectors, who shall verify compliance and investigate violations according to the edict."

sentences.zh: 六年九月，富平縣人梁悅，為父殺仇人秦果，投縣請罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year, Liang Yue of Fuping County killed his father's enemy Qin Guo to avenge him and submitted himself to the district to plead guilty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year, Liang Yue of Fuping County killed Qin Guo to avenge his father's death and surrendered himself to the district magistrate to plead guilty.

sentences.zh: 敕：「復仇殺人，固有彝典。

translations.literal: Edict: "Killing in revenge has its fixed constant law."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Killing in revenge is governed by established law."

sentences.zh: 以其申冤請罪，視死如歸，自詣公門，發於天性。

translations.literal: "Because he declared his grievance and pleaded guilty, viewing death as going home, presenting himself at the public gate—this arose from natural disposition."
translations.idiomatic: "Because he declared his grievance and surrendered himself, facing death as if returning home and coming of his own accord to the public gate—this sprang from natural feeling."

sentences.zh: 志在徇節，本無求生之心，寧失不經，特從減死之法。

translations.literal: "His intent was to follow principle; originally he had no heart to seek life; better to err by not following constant principle—specially apply the law of reduced death."
translations.idiomatic: "His intent was to uphold duty; he had no wish to save his own life. Better to err on the side of mercy than enforce the letter of the law—apply the statute reducing the death penalty."

sentences.zh: 宜決一百，配流循州。

translations.literal: "He should receive one hundred blows and be sentenced to exile in Xunzhou."
translations.idiomatic: "He shall receive one hundred blows and be sentenced to exile in Xunzhou."

sentences.zh: 」職方員外郎韓愈獻議曰：

translations.literal: "Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments Han Yu submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments Han Yu submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 伏奉今月五日敕：復仇，據禮經則義不同天，征法令則殺人者死。

translations.literal: "I humbly received the edict of the fifth day of this month: revenge—according to the ritual classics, the principle differs from Heaven; invoking the legal statutes, one who kills shall die."
translations.idiomatic: "I humbly received the edict of the fifth day of this month on revenge: according to the ritual classics, the duty of vengeance is as great as Heaven itself; according to the legal statutes, one who kills shall die."

sentences.zh: 禮法二事，皆王教之端，有此異同，必資論辯，宜令都省集議聞奏者。

translations.literal: "Ritual and law are two matters, both at the head of royal teaching; having this disagreement necessarily requires debate and argument—it is proper to order the Executive Office to assemble for deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: "Ritual and law are the two foundations of royal teaching. Where they conflict, debate is necessary. It is proper to order the Executive Office to assemble for deliberation and report to the throne."

sentences.zh: 伏以子復父仇，見於《春秋》，見於《禮記》，又見於《周官》，又見於諸子史，不可勝數，未有非而罪之者也。

translations.literal: "I humbly consider that a son avenging his father's murder appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals, appears in the Book of Rites, again appears in the Rites of Zhou, again appears in the various masters and histories—too many to count; never has one been condemned and punished for it."
translations.idiomatic: "I consider that a son avenging his father's murder appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Book of Rites, the Rites of Zhou, and countless other classics and histories. Never has such an act been condemned and punished."

sentences.zh: 最宜詳於律，而律無其條，非闕文也。

translations.literal: "It ought most to be detailed in the statutes, yet the statutes have no such article—this is not a textual lacuna."
translations.idiomatic: "This matter ought above all to be spelled out in the statutes, yet the statutes contain no such article. This is not a textual omission."

sentences.zh: 蓋以為不許復仇，則傷孝子之心，而乖先王之訓；

translations.literal: "The reason is that if revenge were not permitted, it would wound the filial son's heart and violate the former kings' instruction;"
translations.idiomatic: "The reason is that forbidding revenge would wound the filial son's heart and violate the instruction of the former kings;"

sentences.zh: 許復仇，則人將倚法專殺，無以禁止其端矣。

translations.literal: "if revenge were permitted, then people would rely on the law to kill on their own authority, with no means to restrain its beginning."
translations.idiomatic: "but permitting revenge would let people rely on the law to kill on their own authority, with no way to check where that would lead."

sentences.zh: 夫律雖本于聖人，然執而行之者，有司也。

translations.literal: "Although statutes in origin come from the sages, those who hold and execute them are the officials."
translations.idiomatic: "Although the statutes originate with the sages, those who hold and execute them are the officials."

sentences.zh: 經之所明者，制有司也。

translations.literal: "What the classics illuminate is meant to control the officials."
translations.idiomatic: "What the classics illuminate is meant to govern the officials."

sentences.zh: 丁甯其義於經，而深沒其文於律者，其意將使法吏一斷於法，而經術之士，得引經而議也。

translations.literal: "Fixing the meaning in the classics while deeply burying the text in the statutes—the intent is to make legal clerks decide solely by the law, while classical scholars may cite the classics in deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: "By fixing the meaning in the classics while burying the matter deep in the statutes, the intent is to make legal clerks decide solely by the law, while scholars of the classics may cite the classics in deliberation."

sentences.zh: 《周官》曰：「凡殺人而義者，令勿仇，仇之則死。

translations.literal: "The Rites of Zhou says: 'For all who kill someone justly, order that no revenge be taken; if revenge is taken, they die.'"
translations.idiomatic: "The Rites of Zhou says: 'For all who kill someone justly, order that no revenge be taken; if revenge is taken, the avenger dies.'"

sentences.zh: 」義，宜也，明殺人而不得其宜者，子得復仇也。

translations.literal: "'Yi means fittingness—making clear that where one kills a person without obtaining what is fitting, the son may take revenge.'"
translations.idiomatic: "'Yi means fittingness.' This makes clear that where a person is killed without justification, the son may take revenge."

sentences.zh: 此百姓之相仇者也。

translations.literal: "This is common people taking revenge on one another."
translations.idiomatic: "This concerns common people taking revenge on one another."

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》曰：「父不受誅，子復仇可也。

translations.literal: "The Gongyang Commentary says: 'If the father was not subject to execution, the son may take revenge.'"
translations.idiomatic: "The Gongyang Commentary says: 'If the father was not lawfully executed, the son may take revenge.'"

sentences.zh: 」不受誅者，罪不當誅也。

translations.literal: "'Not subject to execution means the crime did not warrant execution.'"
translations.idiomatic: "'Not subject to execution' means the crime did not warrant execution."

sentences.zh: 又《周官》曰：「凡報仇讎者，書於士，殺之無罪。

translations.literal: "Again the Rites of Zhou says: 'For all who repay enmity, register it with the officer; if they kill, there is no crime.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Again the Rites of Zhou says: 'For all who seek to repay a wrong, register it with the officer; if they then kill, there is no crime.'"

sentences.zh: 」言將復仇，必先言於官，則無罪也。

translations.literal: "This means that if one intends revenge, one must first speak to the official, then there is no crime."
translations.idiomatic: "This means that if one intends revenge, one must first inform the authorities; then there is no crime."

sentences.zh: 今陛下垂意典章，思立定制。

translations.literal: "Now Your Majesty turns attention to canonical regulations and thinks to establish fixed institutions."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Your Majesty turns his attention to the canonical regulations and seeks to establish fixed institutions."

sentences.zh: 惜有司之守，憐孝子之心，示不自專，訪議群下。

translations.literal: "Pitying the officials' adherence to law, sympathizing with the filial son's heart, showing that you do not decide alone, you seek deliberation from those below."
translations.idiomatic: "Out of regard for the officials' adherence to law and sympathy for the filial son's heart, you show that you do not decide alone and seek deliberation from your ministers."

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為復仇之名雖同，而其事各異。

translations.literal: "Your servant foolishly considers that though the name of revenge is the same, the matters differ each in their way."
translations.idiomatic: "I consider that though the name of revenge is the same, the cases differ."

sentences.zh: 或百姓相仇，如《周官》所稱，可議於今者；

translations.literal: "Some are common people taking revenge on one another, as the Rites of Zhou speaks of—this may be deliberated for today;"
translations.idiomatic: "Some cases involve common people taking revenge on one another, as the Rites of Zhou describes—these may be considered for the present age;"

sentences.zh: 或為官吏所誅，如《公羊》所稱，不可行於今者。

translations.literal: "some are those executed by officials, as the Gongyang speaks of—this cannot be carried out today."
translations.idiomatic: "others involve those executed by officials, as the Gongyang describes—these cannot be applied today."

sentences.zh: 又《周官》所稱，將復仇，先告於士則無罪者。

translations.literal: "Again what the Rites of Zhou speaks of—if one intends revenge and first informs the officer there is no crime."
translations.idiomatic: "Again, what the Rites of Zhou describes—if one intends revenge and first informs the officer, there is no crime."

sentences.zh: 若孤稚羸弱，抱微志而伺敵人之便，恐不能自言於官，未可以為斷於今也。

translations.literal: "If orphaned, young, weak, and frail, cherishing a small resolve and waiting for the enemy's opportunity, fearing they cannot speak for themselves to the official—this cannot yet be made a rule for today."
translations.idiomatic: "But if one is orphaned, young, weak, and frail, cherishing a small resolve and waiting for the enemy's moment, fearing one cannot speak for oneself to the authorities—this cannot yet be made a fixed rule for today."

sentences.zh: 然則殺之與赦，不可一例。

translations.literal: "Then whether to kill or pardon cannot be one pattern."
translations.idiomatic: "Then whether to execute or pardon cannot be decided by one fixed rule."

sentences.zh: 宜定其制曰：凡有復父仇者，事發，具其事由，下尚書省集議奏聞。

translations.literal: "It is proper to fix the institution thus: wherever there is one who avenges a father's murder, when the matter arises, fully set forth the circumstances of the affair, send down to the Department of State Affairs for assembled deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: "It is proper to establish a rule thus: whenever one avenges a father's murder, when the matter arises, the full circumstances shall be set forth and sent to the Department of State Affairs for assembled deliberation and report to the throne."

sentences.zh: 酌其宜而處之，則經律無失其指矣。

translations.literal: "Weigh what is fitting and dispose accordingly, then the classics and statutes will not lose their aim."
translations.idiomatic: "Weigh what is fitting and dispose accordingly, and the classics and statutes will not lose their true aim."

sentences.zh: 元和十三年八月，鳳翔節度使鄭余慶等詳定《格後敕》三十卷，右司郎中崔郾等六人修上。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang Zheng Yuqing and others finalized thirty fascicles of Post-Regulation Edicts; Right Bureau Director Cui Yan and six others compiled and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang Zheng Yuqing and others finalized thirty fascicles of Post-Regulation Edicts, compiled and submitted by Right Bureau Director Cui Yan and six others.

sentences.zh: 其年，刑部侍郎許孟容、蔣乂等奉詔刪定，復勒成三十卷。

translations.literal: That year, Vice Directors of the Ministry of Justice Xu Mengrong, Jiang Yi, and others received an edict to revise and fix them, again carved into thirty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Vice Directors of the Ministry of Justice Xu Mengrong, Jiang Yi, and others received an edict to revise them and again produced thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎劉伯芻等考定，如其舊卷。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Boxu and others examined and fixed them according to the old fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Boxu and others examined and confirmed them according to the original fascicles.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年五月，御史中丞牛僧孺奏：「天下刑獄，苦於淹滯，請立程限。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Changqing, Vice Censor-in-Chief Niu Sengru memorialized: "Criminal cases throughout the realm suffer from delay and stagnation; I request fixed deadlines be established."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Changqing, Vice Censor-in-Chief Niu Sengru memorialized: "Criminal cases throughout the realm suffer from delay and backlog. I request that fixed deadlines be established."

sentences.zh: 大事，大理寺限三十五日詳斷畢，申刑部，限三十日聞奏。

translations.literal: "For major matters, the Court of Judicial Review is limited to thirty-five days to complete detailed judgment and report to the Ministry of Justice, which is limited to thirty days to report to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: "For major cases, the Court of Judicial Review shall complete detailed judgment within thirty-five days and report to the Ministry of Justice, which shall report to the throne within thirty days."

sentences.zh: 中事，大理寺三十日，刑部二十五日。

translations.literal: "For medium matters, the Court of Judicial Review thirty days, the Ministry of Justice twenty-five days."
translations.idiomatic: "For medium cases, the Court of Judicial Review thirty days, the Ministry of Justice twenty-five days."

sentences.zh: 小事，大理寺二十五日，刑部二十日。

translations.literal: "For minor matters, the Court of Judicial Review twenty-five days, the Ministry of Justice twenty days."
translations.idiomatic: "For minor cases, the Court of Judicial Review twenty-five days, the Ministry of Justice twenty days."

sentences.zh: 一狀所犯十人以上，所斷罪二十件以上，為大。

translations.literal: In one memorial, if the offenders were more than ten persons and the crimes judged were more than twenty items, it was classified as large.
translations.idiomatic: In one memorial, if the offenders numbered more than ten persons and the crimes judged exceeded twenty items, it was classified as large.

sentences.zh: 所犯六人以上，所斷罪十件以上，為中。

translations.literal: If the offenders were more than six persons and the crimes judged were more than ten items, it was classified as medium.
translations.idiomatic: If the offenders numbered more than six persons and the crimes judged exceeded ten items, it was classified as medium.

sentences.zh: 所犯五人以下，所斷罪十件以下，為小。

translations.literal: If the offenders were five persons or fewer and the crimes judged were ten items or fewer, it was classified as small.
translations.idiomatic: If the offenders numbered five persons or fewer and the crimes judged were ten items or fewer, it was classified as small.

sentences.zh: 其或所抵罪狀並所結刑名並同者，則雖人數甚多，亦同一人之例。

translations.literal: If the charged offenses and the fixed punishments were all the same, then even though the number of persons was very great, it was treated by the precedent of a single person.
translations.idiomatic: If the charged offenses and the fixed punishments were all the same, then even though the number of persons was very great, it was treated by the precedent of a single person.

sentences.zh: 違者罪有差。

translations.literal: For violators the punishments had differences in degree.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were punished according to the degree of the offense.

sentences.zh: 」二年四月，刑部員外郎孫革奏：「京兆府雲陽縣人張蒞，欠羽林官騎康憲錢米。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Sun Ge memorialized: "Zhang Li of Yunyang County in the Metropolitan Prefecture owed money and grain to Kang Xian, an officer-rider of the Palace Guards."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Sun Ge memorialized: "Zhang Li of Yunyang County in the Metropolitan Prefecture owed money and grain to Kang Xian, an officer-rider of the Palace Guards."

sentences.zh: 憲征之，蒞承醉拉憲，氣息將絕。

translations.literal: Xian pressed him for payment; Li, taking advantage of drunkenness, seized and pulled Xian, and his breath was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Xian pressed him for payment; Li, taking advantage of drunkenness, seized and pulled Xian until his breath was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 憲男買得，年十四，將救其父。

translations.literal: Xian's son Maidede was fourteen years old and was about to save his father.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Maidede was fourteen years old and sought to save his father.

sentences.zh: 以蒞角牴力人，不敢捴解，遂持木鍤擊蒞之首見血，後三日致死者。

translations.literal: Because Li's horn butting strength was that of a powerful man, he did not dare grapple and release him, but took a wooden spade and struck Li's head until blood appeared; three days later Li died.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li was powerfully built, Maidede did not dare grapple with him, but took a wooden spade and struck Li's head until blood appeared; three days later Li died.

sentences.zh: 准律，父為人所毆，子往救，擊其人折傷，減凡鬥三等。

translations.literal: According to the code, when a father is beaten by another person and the son goes to rescue him and strikes that person causing broken injury, it is reduced three grades from ordinary assault.
translations.idiomatic: According to the code, when a father is beaten by another person and the son goes to rescue him and strikes that person causing broken injury, the offense is reduced three grades from ordinary assault.

sentences.zh: 至死者，依常律。

translations.literal: If it reaches death, the regular code applies.
translations.idiomatic: If death results, the regular code applies.

sentences.zh: 即買得救父難是性孝，非暴；

translations.literal: Thus Maidede's saving his father from peril was filial nature, not violence;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Maidede's saving his father from peril was filial by nature, not violent;

sentences.zh: 擊張蒞是心切，非凶。

translations.literal: striking Zhang Li was heartfelt urgency, not ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: striking Zhang Li was heartfelt urgency, not ferocity.

sentences.zh: 以髫丱之歲，正父子之親，若非聖化所加，童子安能及此？

translations.literal: At the age of childhood topknot, to uphold the intimacy of father and son—if not for the sage transformation bestowed upon him, how could a youth reach this?
translations.idiomatic: At the age of childhood, to uphold the bond of father and son—if not for the sage transformation bestowed upon him, how could a youth reach this?

sentences.zh: 《王制》稱五刑之理，必原父子之親以權之，慎測淺深之量以別之。

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations say that the principle of the five punishments must trace back to the intimacy of father and son to weigh it, and carefully measure the degrees of shallowness and depth to distinguish it.
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations say that the principle of the five punishments must trace back to the intimacy of father and son to weigh it, and carefully measure the degrees of severity to distinguish cases.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，原心定罪。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is to trace the heart to fix guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is to trace the heart to fix guilt.

sentences.zh: 周書所訓，諸罰有權。

translations.literal: What the Book of Zhou instructs is that all punishments have discretionary latitude.
translations.idiomatic: What the Book of Zhou instructs is that all punishments have discretionary latitude.

sentences.zh: 今買得生被皇風，幼符至孝，哀矜之宥，伏在聖慈。

translations.literal: Now Maidede, born under the imperial wind, in youth matched supreme filial piety—the compassionate pardon lies hidden in the sage's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Now Maidede, born under the imperial wind, in youth matched supreme filial piety—compassionate pardon lies in the sage's kindness.

sentences.zh: 臣職當讞刑，合分善惡。

translations.literal: Your servant's duty is to judge punishments and should distinguish good from evil.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's duty is to judge punishments and should distinguish good from evil.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「康買得尚在童年，能知子道，雖殺人當死，而為父可哀。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Kang Maidede is still in childhood and yet knows the way of a son; though killing a man warrants death, acting for his father is pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Kang Maidede is still in childhood and yet knows the way of a son; though killing a man warrants death, acting for his father is pitiable."

sentences.zh: 若從沉命之科，恐失原情之義，宜付法司，減死罪一等。

translations.literal: If the statute of sinking life were followed, one fears losing the meaning of tracing feeling; it is fitting to hand him to the judicial offices and reduce the death offense by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: If the statute of sinking life were followed, one fears losing the meaning of tracing feeling; it is fitting to hand him to the judicial offices and reduce the capital offense by one grade.

sentences.zh: 大和七年十二月，刑部奏：「先奉敕詳定前大理丞謝登《新編格後敕》六十卷者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Dahe, the Ministry of Justice memorialized: "We were previously commanded to examine and fix the sixty scrolls of Newly Compiled Post-Regulation Edicts by former Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xie Deng."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Dahe, the Ministry of Justice memorialized: "We were previously commanded to examine and fix the sixty scrolls of Newly Compiled Post-Regulation Edicts by former Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xie Deng."

sentences.zh: 臣等據謝登所進，詳諸理例，參以格式，或事非久要，恩出一時，或前後差殊，或書寫錯誤，並已落下及改正訖。

translations.literal: Your servants, based on what Xie Deng submitted, examined all principles and precedents and compared them with regulations and forms; matters that were not long-term needs, favors issued for a moment, discrepancies between earlier and later versions, or errors in writing—all have been dropped or corrected to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants, based on what Xie Deng submitted, examined all principles and precedents and compared them with regulations and forms; matters that were not long-term needs, favors issued for a moment, discrepancies between earlier and later versions, or errors in writing—all have been dropped or corrected.

sentences.zh: 去繁舉要，列司分門，都為五十卷。

translations.literal: Removing the cumbersome and raising the essential, listing bureaus by categories, altogether fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the cumbersome and raising the essential, listing bureaus by categories, altogether fifty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 伏請宣下施行。

translations.literal: We humbly request that it be proclaimed and sent down for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly request that it be proclaimed and sent down for implementation.

sentences.zh: 」可之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，詔應犯輕罪人，除情狀巨蠹，法所難原者，其他過誤罪愆，及尋常公事違犯，不得鞭背。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, an edict said that for those who should commit light offenses, except where the circumstances were great corruption and the law could hardly pardon them, all other errors of fault and guilt, and ordinary violations in official business, could not be flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year, an edict said that for those who should commit light offenses, except where the circumstances were great corruption and the law could hardly pardon them, all other errors of fault and guilt, and ordinary violations in official business, could not be flogged on the back.

sentences.zh: 遵太宗之故事也。

translations.literal: This followed the precedent of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: This followed the precedent of Taizong.

sentences.zh: 俄而京兆尹韋長奏：「京師浩穰，奸豪所聚。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Metropolitan Prefect Wei Chang memorialized: "The capital is vast and crowded, a gathering place for villains and powerful men."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Metropolitan Prefect Wei Chang memorialized: "The capital is vast and crowded, a gathering place for villains and powerful men."

sentences.zh: 終日懲罰，抵犯猶多，小有寬容，即難禁戢。

translations.literal: Punishment all day long, yet offenders are still numerous; if there is slight leniency, it is immediately hard to restrain and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment all day long, yet offenders are still numerous; if there is slight leniency, it is immediately hard to restrain and suppress.

sentences.zh: 若恭守敕旨，則無以肅清；

translations.literal: If we respectfully obey the edict, there is no way to achieve order and purity;
translations.idiomatic: If we respectfully obey the edict, there is no way to achieve order and purity;

sentences.zh: 若臨事用刑，則有違詔使。

translations.literal: if we apply punishments when handling affairs, we violate the edict's command.
translations.idiomatic: if we apply punishments when handling affairs, we violate the edict's command.

sentences.zh: 伏望許依前據輕重處置。

translations.literal: We humbly hope to be permitted to dispose according to severity and leniency as before.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly hope to be permitted to dispose according to severity and leniency as before.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，兩省詳定《刑法格》一十卷，敕令施行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, the two departments examined and fixed the Penal Regulations in ten scrolls, and an edict ordered them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, the two departments examined and fixed the Penal Regulations in ten scrolls, and an edict ordered them into effect.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年九月，庫部郎中、知制誥紇幹泉等奏：「准刑部奏，犯贓官五品已上，合抵死刑，請准獄官令死於家者，伏請永為定格。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Huichang, Bureau Director of the Storehouse and Drafter of Edicts Qian Ganquan and others memorialized: "According to the Ministry of Justice's memorial, corrupt officials of the fifth grade and above who should receive the death penalty—requesting approval of the prison officials' ordinance that they die at home—we humbly request this be made a permanent regulation forever."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Huichang, Bureau Director of the Storehouse and Drafter of Edicts Qian Ganquan and others memorialized: "According to the Ministry of Justice's memorial, corrupt officials of the fifth grade and above who should receive the death penalty—requesting approval of the prison officials' ordinance that they die at home—we humbly request this be made a permanent regulation forever."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 大中五年四月，刑部侍郎劉彖等奉敕修《大中刑法總要格後敕》六十卷，起貞觀二年六月二十日，至大中五年四月十三日，凡二百二十四年雜敕，都計六百四十六門，二千一百六十五條。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Dazhong, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yan and others received command to compile the Dazhong General Essentials of Penal Law Post-Regulation Edicts in sixty scrolls, from the twentieth day of the sixth month of the second year of Zhenguan to the thirteenth day of the fourth month of the fifth year of Dazhong—altogether two hundred twenty-four years of miscellaneous edicts, totaling six hundred forty-six categories and two thousand one hundred sixty-five articles.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Dazhong, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yan and others received command to compile the Dazhong General Essentials of Penal Law Post-Regulation Edicts in sixty scrolls, from the twentieth day of the sixth month of the second year of Zhenguan to the thirteenth day of the fourth month of the fifth year of Dazhong—altogether two hundred twenty-four years of miscellaneous edicts, totaling six hundred forty-six categories and two thousand one hundred sixty-five articles.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，左衛率倉曹參軍張戣進《大中刑法統類》一十二卷，敕刑部詳定奏行之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Staff Officer of the Left Guard Rate Granary Bureau Zhang Kai presented the Dazhong Penal Law Classified Compendium in twelve scrolls; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to examine, fix, memorialize, and put it into practice.
